papers.title: Vestibular Epilepsy Presenting With Isolated Recurrent Vertigo and Postictal Headache: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Vestibular epilepsy, also referred to as epileptic vertigo syndrome, is a rare and underrecognized cause of recurrent episodic vertigo. Currently, there are no universally accepted diagnostic criteria for vestibular epilepsy. A 38-year-old woman presented with an eight-month history of recurrent spontaneous episodes of rotational vertigo lasting one to two minutes and occurring multiple times daily. Episodes were accompanied by nausea and vomiting and were followed by bilateral throbbing headaches. Neurological examination, bedside vestibular assessment, and cognitive screening were unremarkable. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated no structural epileptogenic lesion, while brainstem evoked response audiometry was normal. Electroencephalography revealed frequent generalized epileptiform discharges with a photoparoxysmal response during intermittent photic stimulation. The patient was diagnosed with vestibular epilepsy with postictal headache after exclusion of alternative causes of episodic vertigo. Treatment with extended-release divalproex sodium resulted in a marked reduction in attack frequency and improvement in symptoms during follow-up. Vestibular epilepsy represents an uncommon seizure manifestation in which vestibular symptoms predominate and may occur in isolation. In this patient, the brief stereotyped attacks, normal brain neuroimaging, absence of peripheral vestibular abnormalities, epileptiform electroencephalographic findings, and favorable response to antiseizure therapy supported the diagnosis. In cases of recurrent episodic vertigo presenting concurrently with headache, vestibular epilepsy remains a diagnostic challenge, mainly because overt neurological manifestations are often absent. Recent literature suggests that electroencephalography should be considered in patients with recurrent unexplained brief vertigo, particularly when episodes are stereotyped or resistant to conventional vestibular therapies.

papers.title: NADPH phosphatase activity of Mesh1 contributes to sleep regulation in Drosophila.
papers.abstract: Metazoans possess Mesh1, an enzyme with both ppGpp hydrolase and NADPH phosphatase activities, raising questions about their respective physiological roles. To distinguish these functions, we combined biochemical characterization, structure-guided mutagenesis, genome editing, and behavioral analysis in Drosophila. We found that Drosophila Mesh1 dephosphorylates NADPH but not NADP+ in vitro. Substitution of tryptophan 138 with phenylalanine (W138F) abolished detectable NADPH phosphatase activity while retaining detectable but severely reduced ppGpp hydrolase activity. Flies carrying the W138F mutation exhibited reduced total sleep duration and increased sleep fragmentation. These findings implicate the NADPH phosphatase activity of Mesh1 in sleep regulation and identify W138 as a critical residue for this function. Our results highlight a physiological role for Mesh1 beyond ppGpp metabolism and suggest a connection between NADPH metabolism and the regulation of sleep in metazoans.

papers.title: Childhood abuse is linked to poor sleep in adult women.
papers.abstract: Women are disproportionately affected by poor sleep, both in terms of quantity and quality. One relatively unexplored association with poor sleep is adverse childhood experiences, which also disproportionately affect women. Prior research treats all adverse experiences as equivalent, focusing on the number of adverse events rather than the types of adversity experienced. This cumulative focus, while valuable for identifying dose-dependent responses, overlooks how different adversities are detrimental for women's health. We investigated how adversity contributed to sleep issues in a sample of treatment-seeking women (N=350). Survey measures collected participants' demographic information, adverse childhood experiences (ACEs), and sleep quantity and quality. We used cumulative and dimensional person-centered analytic approaches, the latter of which revealed four distinct adversity subgroups and two distinct sleep subgroups. Women having experienced abuse-related adversity (emotional and/or physical) as well as multiple forms of adversity (high cumulative scores) were more likely to experience worse sleep. Those experiencing abuse experienced sleep issues even when their cumulative adversity scores did not reach clinical thresholds. Women classified within household dysfunction and low cumulative scores did not report deleterious sleep. Findings suggest that specific patterns of childhood adversity uniquely contribute to adult sleep issues among women. These women are not captured in cumulative scoring methods, potentially leading to their abuse histories being overlooked in clinical settings. This study underscores the importance of using dimensional approaches to ACE research and highlights the enduring impact of childhood adversity on women's sleep health.

papers.title: Latent profile analysis of sleep quality and associated factors in Chinese adolescents with major depressive disorder.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are pervasive among adolescent patients with major depressive disorder (MDD), yet the heterogeneity of sleep phenotypes within this population remains underexplored. This study aimed to identify latent profiles of sleep quality in Chinese adolescent patients with MDD and to examine their associations with sociodemographic, clinical, and psychosocial factors. A total of 1,467 adolescent patients with MDD were assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), the Borderline Personality Features Scale for Children (BPFS-C), and a self-designed sociodemographic and clinical inventory. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was conducted using the seven PSQI component scores as profile indicators. Multinomial logistic regression was subsequently performed to determine factors associated with profile membership. A five-profile solution was identified: Normal Sleep Group (13%), Mild Disturbance-Low Hypnotic Use (36%), Mild Disturbance-High Hypnotic Use (22%), Severe Disturbance-Low Hypnotic Use (16%), and Severe Disturbance-High Hypnotic Use (13%). Logistic regression revealed that the presence of non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) and exposure to negative life events significantly increased the odds of belonging to more severe sleep disturbance profiles (OR = 2.92-8.37 and 2.33-2.60, respectively; all p < 0.05). Notably, patients without left-behind experiences exhibited higher odds of being classified into the Severe Disturbance-High Hypnotic Use profile compared to those with such histories (OR = 0.46, p < 0.001). Furthermore, profiles characterized by poorer sleep quality and profiles characterized by more frequent self-reported sleep medication use were cross-sectionally associated with greater anxiety and borderline features in this study. Sleep quality among adolescent patients with MDD exhibits distinct typological heterogeneity, characterized primarily by severity and hypnotic use patterns. These findings provide preliminary exploratory evidence for the development of personalized, profile-informed clinical interventions for this vulnerable population.

papers.title: Could excessive infant mattress firmness contribute to positional plagiocephaly in Japan? An international comparison and hypothesis paper.
papers.abstract: International infant sleep-surface standards primarily address the prevention of overly soft sleep surfaces using pass/fail test methods rather than specifying a directly comparable consumer firmness value in Newtons. No international standard establishes an upper firmness limit for infant mattresses. Japan has no infant-specific national mattress firmness standard. To document the firmness (Newton value, N) of Japanese commercially available infant mattresses, compare these values against international regulatory frameworks and selected manufacturer recommendations, and propose a biomechanical hypothesis suggesting that excessive mattress firmness may contribute to the apparently higher prevalence of positional plagiocephaly (PP) reported in Japanese cohorts. Firmness values (N; JIS K6400-2 Method A, 40% compression) were collected from publicly available manufacturer or retailer specifications for ten Japanese infant mattress products satisfying pre-defined inclusion criteria (the primary analysis dataset). Two additional products, identified outside the original search during revision, are reported as a sensitivity check only. International reference values were obtained from regulatory documents, selected European manufacturer guidance, and product documentation. PP prevalence data were extracted from peer-reviewed literature; cross-national comparisons are presented as illustrative only. Japanese infant mattress firmness ranged from 160 to 285 N (median 183 N, ten-product primary analysis). No direct numerical comparison with European density-based manufacturer recommendations is made, as no validated conversion between density (kg/m3) and ILD firmness (N) exists. Five products had firmness at or below 176 N; four products exceeded 190 N. Of the ten products, six fell within the Korean reference-test-mattress specification range (170 ± 20 N = 150-190 N), indicating that the Japanese market does not consist uniformly of extreme outliers. This preliminary survey is restricted to ten products identified through publicly accessible manufacturer or retailer specifications; independent laboratory verification was not performed. Existing evidence strongly supports firm sleep surfaces as a key measure for reducing sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS) risk. The present hypothesis concerns only the upper end of the firmness spectrum-specifically, whether surfaces that are excessively firm may carry biomechanical consequences distinct from those of appropriately firm surfaces. This paper does not recommend using softer mattresses, adding comfort toppers, or using positioning pillows or positioners. Excessive mattress firmness may reduce occipital contact surface area (increasing interfacial pressure: P = F/A) and may reduce small spontaneous head-position changes during sleep (a direction that remains to be tested), thereby increasing sustained focal pressure on the immature, malleable calvaria and potentially contributing to the apparently higher PP prevalence reported in Japan. Japanese infant mattresses surveyed had a median firmness of 183 N. Among the regulatory frameworks reviewed, Japan lacks an infant-specific national mattress firmness standard, and no international standard establishes an upper firmness limit. Independent market-wide testing and prospective outcome studies are warranted to determine whether an infant-specific upper firmness range should be considered.

papers.title: Impulse Oscilometry in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Is it Useful?
papers.abstract: Oscillometry is a non-invasive method for assessing the impedance (Z) of the respiratory system, which depends on resistance (R) and reactance (X). Currently, it is mainly developed in obstructive diseases and its utility in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) remains unclear. In a few previous studies it has been explored as a diagnostic tool for OSA with positive findings, but most included obese individuals, making it unclear whether observed changes were due to OSA or obesity. Our study aimed to evaluate oscillometry values specifically in non-obese patients with and without OSA to clarify these relationships without the confounding effect of obesity, as well as to describe these parameters based on disease severity. We conducted a prospective observational study at Getafe University Hospital (Madrid) between January and December 2023. A total of 60 patients, aged 18-75 years, who attended the sleep disorders consultation were recruited: 30 with OSA and 30 without OSA, confirmed by polygraphy. All participants underwent oscillometry to measure respiratory resistance (Rrs) and reactance (Xrs) at different frequencies. Results, adjusted for age, sex, and BMI, revealed no statistically significant differences in resistance or reactance between groups. Furthermore, no correlation was found between oscillometric parameters and OSA severity. In the course of our study, we did not observe significant mechanical alterations, suggesting that in non-obese individuals, basal respiratory mechanics remain preserved during wakefulness. These findings support the need to consider obesity as a potential confounding factor when interpreting oscillometric abnormalities previously reported in patients with OSA. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Prevalence of physical activity, sedentary screen time, and sleep duration among non-Saudi adolescents in Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Non-Saudi residents constitute nearly 44% of Saudi Arabia's population, yet non-Saudi adolescents have been almost entirely absent from national school-health surveillance, including studies using the Global School-based Student Health Survey (GSHS). This study aimed to determine the prevalence of physical activity, sedentary screen time, and sleep duration among non-Saudi adolescents across five Saudi cities, and to examine variation by sex and city of residence. A cross-sectional survey using a modified, Arabic-translated GSHS questionnaire was administered to students in 40 public intermediate schools across Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam, Khamis Mushait, and Tabuk. This analysis was restricted to non-Saudi students with complete data (n = 1,036). Physical activity (linear regression) and three binary outcomes, 7-day activity attainment, high sedentary screen time, and very short sleep (logistic regression) were each modeled with sex, city of residence, and age as simultaneous covariates, using cluster-robust standard errors to account for students nested within 36 schools. Adjusted estimates and 95% confidence intervals are reported, with a Bonferroni-corrected threshold (α = 0.006) applied across eight tests (sex and city for each of four outcomes). Only 14.0% of participants reported ≥60 min of physical activity on all 7 days, 26.8% reported no active days, 48.9% reported high sedentary screen time, and 37.1% reported very short sleep duration (≤6 h, below the 8-10 h recommended for this age group). After adjustment for city, age, and school clustering, males reported more physical activity days than females (adjusted mean difference = 0.66 days/week, 95% CI 0.23-1.09, p = 0.003) and were less likely to report very short sleep (aOR = 0.59, 95% CI 0.47-0.74, p < 0.001); both associations survived Bonferroni correction. Males were also more likely to report ≥60 min of activity on all 7 days (aOR = 1.55, p = 0.035) and less likely to report high sedentary screen time (aOR = 0.74, p = 0.012), but neither survived correction. City of residence was not significantly associated with physical activity days, high sedentary time, or very short sleep, but showed a nominally significant, non-corrected association with 7-day activity attainment (driven by Dammam vs. Riyadh). Older age was independently associated with fewer physical activity days (adjusted difference = -0.14 days/year, p = 0.036). Physical inactivity, high sedentary screen time, and very short sleep were common among non-Saudi adolescents attending public schools in Saudi Arabia. Sex differences were robust for physical activity days and short sleep, while differences in 7-day activity attainment and sedentary time were smaller and did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. City of residence contributed little to this variation. These findings, among the first population-specific estimates for this substantial and previously understudied group, support further surveillance and consideration of non-Saudi students in school health programming; the effectiveness of sex-specific interventions should be evaluated in future research rather than assumed from these cross-sectional findings.

papers.title: Spikes in the night: rapid eye movement sleep maximally attenuates epileptiform spike morphology.
papers.abstract: To characterize morphological differences in interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) across sleep-wake states (rapid eye movement (REM), Non-REM1-3, wakefulness). Prospectively analyzed 7379 IEDs from 17 adults with focal epilepsy (12 unifocal, 5 multifocal) admitted to an epilepsy monitoring unit for continuous surface video-EEG telemetry (41.8±17.2 years, 52.9% females) using custom-developed software allowing manual confirmation of IEDs and sleep-wake states. Nine morphological IED features reflecting paroxysmal depolarizing shift dynamics and magnitude were quantified across three EEG montages (raw, referential and Laplacian). Nonparametric Kruskal-Wallis and post hoc Dunn-Sidak tests with Bonferroni correction assessed state-dependent differences. Only features surviving correction across all montages were considered reproducibly significant. IED morphology varied significantly by state (p < 10-12-10-134). Across all montages and subgroups, REM IEDs had shallowest slopes (upslope 2.91-4.22 μV/s; downslope 2.87-4.33 μV/s), bluntest peaks (27.04°-40.24°), and shortest amplitudes and smallest area, (multifocal-driven). Awake IEDs had steepest slopes (upslope 8.97-15.23 μV/s; downslope 7.54-13.84 μV/s), and spikiest peaks (8.18°-14.44°). NREM IEDs were intermediate. Epileptiform morphology in REM was most attenuated. Shallower slopes, blunter peaks, shorter, and smaller-area IEDs indicate an electrobiological milieu less promoting of epileptic activity than NREM's synchronized state or wakefulness's maximally responsive state. Despite REM and wakefulness being desynchronized on surface EEG, REM's morphological IED divergence raises future directions into sui generis anti-epileptic mechanisms, including network connectivity and pH-responsive orexinergic glial dynamics. The sleep-wake cycle strongly modulates epileptic activity, yet seizures rarely arise from REM (~1%). However, REM contains sufficient IEDs to characterize morphology and probe potential anti-epileptic solutions via their underlying cellular mechanisms.

papers.title: Office blood pressure measurement versus ambulatory blood pressure monitoring for detecting undiagnosed hypertension in an apparently healthy Mexican adult cohort: complementary central hemodynamic and arterial stiffness assessment.
papers.abstract: Office blood pressure measurement is widely used for hypertension screening, but its diagnostic performance is limited by blood pressure variability and white-coat or masked hypertension. Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) provides a more comprehensive assessment, including nighttime blood pressure and circadian patterns. Central aortic pressure (CAP) and arterial stiffness parameters may provide complementary information on vascular hemodynamics. To evaluate the diagnostic performance of office blood pressure measurement for detecting previously undiagnosed hypertension using composite ABPM as the reference standard, and to describe ABPM-derived phenotypes, circadian blood pressure patterns, and central hemodynamic and arterial stiffness parameters. This cross-sectional analytical study included 151 adults without a previous diagnosis of hypertension. Participants underwent office blood pressure measurement, 24-hour ABPM, and noninvasive assessment of CAP and arterial stiffness. Composite ABPM hypertension was defined as 24-hour blood pressure >130/80 mmHg, daytime blood pressure >135/85 mmHg, or nighttime blood pressure >120/70 mmHg. Office blood pressure measurement identified hypertension in 15 participants (9.9%), whereas composite ABPM identified hypertension in 29 (19.2%). Masked hypertension was observed in 18 participants (11.9%) and white-coat hypertension in 4 (2.6%). Nighttime hypertension was present in 29 participants (19.2%). Office blood pressure measurement showed low sensitivity (37.9%) and high specificity (96.7%) for composite ABPM hypertension. The dipper phenotype was observed in 80 participants (53.0%), non-dipper in 59 (39.1%), riser in 6 (4.0%), and extreme dipper in 6 (4.0%). Mean CAP was 120.7 ± 20.4 mmHg, and elevated pulse wave velocity >10 m/s was observed in 9 participants (6.0%). Office blood pressure measurement underestimated the prevalence of hypertension compared with composite ABPM. ABPM identified masked, nighttime, and circadian blood pressure abnormalities that were not detected by office measurements. CAP, AIx, and PWV provided complementary exploratory information on central hemodynamic and arterial stiffness markers.

papers.title: From efficacy verification to precision intervention: a dual-database bibliometric and clinical mapping analysis of therapeutic exercise for adolescent obesity (2016-2025).
papers.abstract: This study aimed to systematically map the research landscape, knowledge structure, collaboration patterns, and evolutionary frontiers of therapeutic exercise for adolescent obesity from 2016 to 2025, and to identify translational gaps between basic research and clinical practice. Publications were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and PubMed. The WoSCC dataset, comprising original articles and reviews, was analyzed using CiteSpace 7.0.1 for co-citation, keyword co-occurrence, thematic clustering, and burst detection, and VOSviewer 1.6.19 for collaboration networks at the country, institution, and author levels. The PubMed dataset, restricted to clinical research, was analyzed using CiteSpace to identify clinical intervention hotspots and evolutionary trends. A total of 2,953 records from WoSCC and 1,295 clinical studies from PubMed were included. Annual publications showed a fluctuating upward trend, peaking at 349 articles in 2022. The United States and China led publication output, but international cross-regional collaboration remained limited, with high-output countries functioning primarily as production cores rather than collaboration hubs. Ten research clusters were identified in the WoSCC dataset, with insulin resistance, cardiorespiratory fitness, and body mass index as core themes. Research evolved through three distinct phases: basic efficacy evaluation (2016-2018), mechanism and benefit expansion (2019-2021), and precision intervention for special populations (2022-2025). Clinical research in PubMed emphasized intervention efficacy and patient-oriented outcomes, with high-intensity interval training and health-related quality of life emerging as the latest frontiers since 2024. A clear thematic divergence was observed between basic research, which focused on mechanistic targets and population characteristics, and clinical practice, which prioritized intervention protocols and practical outcomes. Therapeutic exercise research for adolescent obesity has developed steadily from 2016 to 2025, with prominent multidisciplinary integration but insufficient international cross-regional collaboration. A potential translational gap, reflected by thematic divergence, persists between basic mechanistic research and clinical practice. Future efforts should prioritize multi-factor synergistic interventions combining exercise with sleep, nutrition, and psychological support; precision exercise prescriptions tailored to special populations such as adolescents with Down syndrome or severe obesity; and high-quality multicenter clinical trials to accelerate the translation of basic findings into standardized clinical protocols.

papers.title: Shared mechanisms and therapeutic horizons: exploring the potential interplay between benign prostatic hyperplasia/lower urinary tract symptoms and Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) are two prevalent age-related disorders with significant global healthcare burdens. Traditionally viewed as distinct conditions, emerging evidence suggests that they may share common pathophysiological mechanisms, including chronic inflammation, endocrine dysregulation, metabolic dysfunction, cardiovascular impairment, and sleep disturbances. This review synthesizes current epidemiological, mechanistic, and therapeutic insights linking BPH and AD, with a focus on their overlapping risk factors and molecular pathways. Although most of the currently available evidence is observational and cannot establish causality, understanding these interactions could inform novel preventive and therapeutic strategies to mitigate the dual burden of neurodegenerative and urological conditions in older populations.

papers.title: Seizure Prediction Using Channel-Optimized Intracranial EEG With Variable Interictal and Preictal Durations.
papers.abstract: Objective: Predicting epileptic seizures using electroencephalogram (EEG) signals can provide a critical window for intervention to suppress impending seizures. However, the impact of varying interictal and preictal durations on seizure prediction remains unclear and warrants further exploration. Considering this, this study focuses on seizure prediction using intracranial EEG (iEEG) signals with variable interictal and preictal durations. Method: In this work, we discuss six pairwise combinations in total, involving two interictal durations (24 h and 48 h) and three preictal durations (30 min, 60 min and 90 min), during seizure prediction analysis. Furthermore, we also compare three classification strategies: the all-channel strategy (Strategy 1), the single-channel-based majority voting strategy (Strategy 2) and the channel-optimization-based majority voting strategy (Strategy 3), across each pairwise combination. Results: The long-term SWEC-ETHZ iEEG dataset is utilized to evaluate our method. The results reveal that our method achieves up to 87.7 sensitivity, 94.6 specificity, 92.8 accuracy, 0.912 Area Under the Curve (AUC) and 0.858 F1-score at the segment-based level, along with 95.9 sensitivity and 0.05/h false prediction rate (FPR) at the event-based level. Moreover, the overall performance of Strategy 3 surpasses that of Strategies 1 and 2 in each pairwise combination, indicating that channel optimization is beneficial for improving seizure prediction performance. Conclusion: This work shows high effectiveness in predicting seizures using iEEG signals, with the ability to forecast upcoming epileptic events up to 90 min in advance across both 24-h and 48-h interictal durations.
papers.journal: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology

papers.title: Group-specific associations among sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and frontal alpha asymmetry in college students: evidence from a cross-sectional EEG study.
papers.abstract: Poor sleep quality is associated with depressive symptoms, but its accompanying neurophysiological correlates remain unclear in non-clinical college students. This study examined associations among sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and frontal alpha asymmetry (FAA) in students with and without elevated depressive symptoms. This cross-sectional study included 120 college students, comprising 60 students with depressive symptoms (DS) and 60 non-depressed controls (NC), classified using the Self-Rating Depression Scale. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and FAA was derived from resting-state EEG. Analyses included BMI-adjusted group comparisons, partial correlations, regression models, and an exploratory indirect-path analysis. False discovery rate correction was applied to multiple comparisons. After BMI adjustment, the DS group had higher PSQI scores [median (P25, P75): 7 (6, 10) vs. 3 (1, 5)] and lower composite FAA values [-0.041 (-0.116, 0.031) vs. 0.056 (0.017, 0.103); both p < 0.001] than the NC group. Similar FAA differences were observed using frontopolar and frontal electrode-pair indices. PSQI scores were positively correlated with depressive symptoms in both groups (DS: r = 0.412, q = 0.006; NC: r = 0.462, q = 0.001). In the DS group, composite FAA was negatively correlated with PSQI (r = -0.322, q = 0.034) and depressive symptoms (r = -0.388, q = 0.010); neither FAA-related association reached statistical significance in the NC group. After BMI adjustment, PSQI and FAA were jointly associated with depressive symptom severity in the DS group (R 2 = 0.243). An exploratory indirect-path analysis yielded an indirect association estimate of 0.092 (95% bootstrap CI: 0.002-0.202). Poorer sleep quality was associated with greater depressive symptom severity in both groups, whereas FAA-related associations were observed mainly in the DS group. These findings suggest that FAA may be a candidate neurophysiological correlate of the concurrent association between sleep quality and depressive symptoms in non-clinical college students. Causal mediation cannot be inferred from this cross-sectional study.

papers.title: Altered interhemispheric functional cooperation in persistent postural-perceptual dizziness.
papers.abstract: Persistent postural-perceptual dizziness (PPPD) is associated with altered multisensory processing, but its hemispheric functional organization remains poorly understood. We investigated hemispheric functional lateralization and interhemispheric cooperation in PPPD and explored their associations with clinical symptoms and neurotransmitter density maps. A total of 47 patients with PPPD and 52 healthy controls (HCs) underwent resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. Whole-brain maps of the autonomy index (AI) and connectivity between functionally homotopic voxels (CFH) were generated. Between-group differences were assessed using permutation-based analyses adjusted for age, sex, and mean framewise displacement (FD). Associations with clinical measures and spatial correspondence with 13 neurotransmitter density maps were also examined. The PPPD and HC groups did not differ significantly in age, sex, or educational level (all p > 0.05). Patients with PPPD had lower MoCA-BJ scores and higher HAMA-14, HAMD-24, PSQI, and DHI scores than HCs, whereas MMSE scores did not differ significantly. No between-group differences in AI survived family-wise error (FWE) correction. By contrast, in the primary analysis, patients with PPPD showed significantly reduced CFH in the right calcarine cortex, right cuneus, left inferior and middle occipital gyri, left inferior parietal lobule, and right middle temporal gyrus. However, no CFH clusters survived cluster-level FWE correction after separately adjusting for HAMA-14, HAMD-24, or PSQI scores. After adjustment for age, sex, and mean FD, CFH in the right calcarine cortex and left inferior parietal lobule showed negative associations with DHI total and DHI-E scores, respectively (Shepherd's π = -0.363 and -0.452), but neither association remained significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. The CFH group-difference map showed nominal positive spatial correlations with the D2R and VAChT density maps, but these associations were not significant after FDR correction. In primary analysis, PPPD patients exhibited reduced interhemispheric functional cooperation in visual, visuospatial and multisensory regions, while no AI differences survived FWE correction. However, these CFH findings were sensitive to adjustment for affective symptoms and sleep quality; the relative contributions of PPPD, affective symptoms and sleep disturbance remain uncertain. Clinical and neurotransmitter density-map associations did not survive FDR correction and are exploratory.

papers.title: Circadian vulnerability in acute myocardial infarction: from clock-regulated pathways to chrono-individualized therapy.
papers.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and its onset, progression, and prognosis are closely tied to circadian rhythms. Disruption of the biological clock influences susceptibility to AMI as well as the pathophysiological mechanisms and therapeutic responses that follow. This review examines how circadian regulation shapes thrombogenesis, ischemia-reperfusion injury, cardiac metabolism, inflammation, and myocardial repair, spanning the molecular architecture of the cardiomyocyte clock, the early-morning peak in AMI incidence, and the circadian control of platelet function, fibrinolysis, mitochondrial integrity, substrate selection, calcium handling, and the inflammatory response. Building on these mechanisms, we outline chrono-individualized therapy-the alignment of prevention and long-term management with an individual's measured internal circadian phase, as distinct from fixed-clock-time chronotherapy-and present it deliberately as a research agenda rather than an implementable clinical pathway. In the emergency setting, where reperfusion must never be delayed, we argue that circadian biology should inform risk stratification and the intensity of monitoring rather than the timing of intervention. We set out the principal bottlenecks: no validated point-of-care assay of circadian phase exists, and the correspondence between peripheral blood clock-gene phase and the cardiac clock is unestablished; indirect phase estimation from wearable data is the most tractable workaround. The largest randomized trial of cardiovascular dose timing was neutral, and no event-driven trial has yet shown that aligning therapy to circadian phase improves outcomes after AMI, so the present case for chronotherapy rests principally on mechanistic and observational data.

papers.title: EFFECT OF A GROUP OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY INTERVENTION ON DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS, LEVEL OF OCCUPATIONAL PARTICIPATION AND FUNCTIONING AMONG IN-SCHOOL ADOLESCENTS IN ABEOKUTA, NIGERIA.
papers.abstract: Impairment in occupational participation and functioning can negatively affect adolescents' activities of daily living, academic performance, self-care, sleep, leisure, and mood. This study examined the effects of a structured occupational therapy intervention on mood, occupational functioning, and social participation among in-school adolescents with depressive symptoms. A two-stage design was employed, comprising a crosssectional survey followed by a one-group pre?post intervention study. In the first stage, 345 students from four schools completed the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI). Ten students with scores of 18 and above were recruited into the intervention phase and completed the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM), Short Mood and Feelings Questionnaire (SMFQ), and Wellness and Life Satisfaction Questionnaire. A five-week manualised occupational therapy programme was delivered, and complete pre?post data from ten participants were analysed. The mean age of participants was 14.9 ± 1.2 years, and 26.1% scored within the significant depressive symptom range. Females reported higher depressive symptoms than males (p = 0.02) and the mean BDI score for the screened sample was 11.61 (SD = 10.23). Post-intervention analysis showed significant reductions in depressive symptoms and improvements in occupational functioning and social participation, with large effect sizes. These findings suggest that school-based occupational therapy interventions are feasible and may improve functional and emotional outcomes among adolescents with depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Differential effects of β1- and β2-adrenergic receptor block in long QT syndrome type 3: an in silico population study.
papers.abstract: Long QT syndrome type 3 (LQT3) is caused by a gain-of-function mutation in the voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.5, resulting in an increased late sodium current (INaL) that prolongs action potential duration (APD) and promotes the development of early afterdepolarizations (EAD). LQT3 is commonly treated with therapies involving β-adrenergic receptor blockers. However, recent studies suggest that β-blockers may not provide a beneficial clinical effect in LQT3 patients, potentially explaining the increased risk of mortality during cardiac events compared to other long QT subtypes. This study investigates the underlying mechanisms of selective β-receptor block using a population-based computational approach. A population of 983 virtual human ventricular myocytes with enhanced INaL (representing LQT3) simulated, enabling electrophysiological and β-adrenergic analysis under conditions of varying degrees of β1- and β2-block. Susceptibility to arrhythmic events was quantified via APD prolongation or occurrence of EADs, and differences in susceptibility pathways, phosphorylation states, and ion current conductances were analyzed between susceptible and non-susceptible subpopulations. Our results demonstrate that β1-block increases susceptibility, primarily via reduced IKs phosphorylation. In contrast, full β2-block reduces susceptibility, primarily via reduced ICaL phosphorylation, while partial β2-block does not. Differences in ionic current conductances in the susceptible and non-susceptible sub-populations are consistent with β-block driving imbalances in depolarizing and repolarizing currents. Our findings motivate the development and preclinical testing of more selective β2-blocking agents, which could improve therapeutic outcomes in LQT3 patients.

papers.title: Predictive modeling of sleep quality during health crises: a primary dataset from COVID-19 among Bangladeshi population.
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic had a significant impact on sleep health globally, and developing nations like Bangladesh has added complexity due to population density, socio-economic issues, and a lack of mental health resources. This article shares a primary dataset from 945 respondents (59.2% male, 40.8% female) in Bangladesh for use in research studies on sleep health during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The dataset includes socio-demographic and socioeconomic variables, lifestyle, behavioral and COVID-19 related variables, and sleep and insomnia related variables, such as Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) responses. The data was gathered by using a structured questionnaire, and then preprocessed using cleaning, encoding, and validation procedures to ensure consistency and usability of the data. To describe the study population and structure of the data set descriptive statistics are applied. This freely accessible data may be useful for future research in public health, sleep medicine, epidemiology, behavioral science, mental health, and for data-driven studies of sleep-related outcomes in the Global South.

papers.title: Factors associated with cancer-related fatigue in breast cancer patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Cancer-related fatigue (CRF) remains one of the most common and persistent complications among breast cancer survivors, profoundly impairing their psychosocial well-being. Although various predictors have been proposed, existing evidence yields inconsistent findings. This study aimed to systematically synthesize multidimensional factors associated with CRF in this population, providing an evidence-based framework for identifying the individuals and tailoring early interventions. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library and Web of Science databases for studies investigating factors associated with fatigue in breast cancer patients, The search covered the period from database inception to May 3, 2026. Two researchers independently performed study screening, quality assessment, and data extraction, and statistical analyses were performed using Stata 19.0. 16 studies involving a total of 11,984 patients were included. Some potentially relevant factors were identified: pain (OR 1.78, 95% CI 1.29-2.45), dyspnea (OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.10-3.66), anxiety (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.12-1.86), depression (OR 1.97, 95% CI 1.49-2.60), sleep disturbances (OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.05-3.87) and BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2 (OR 1.36, 95% CI 1.05-1.75). The patients with cancer- related fatigue in breast cancer, pain, dyspnea, anxiety, depression, sleep disturbances (OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.05-3.87) and BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2 may be associated with fatigue and should be considered as potential related factors. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261432176.

papers.title: Adjunctive delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol during prolonged exposure therapy for PTSD: A randomized, double-blind feasibility pilot trial with mechanistic assessment of extinction recall.
papers.abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a chronic and debilitating condition. Delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) has been shown to influence fear extinction learning and recall, providing a mechanistic rationale for its use as an adjunct to exposure-based therapy. We conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot feasibility trial evaluating low-dose oral THC administered during Prolonged Exposure (PE) therapy for PTSD. Twenty-three adults with PTSD completed massed PE delivered via telehealth and were randomized to receive either 7.5 mg oral dronabinol (THC) or placebo prior to PE sessions 3-6. Primary outcomes included clinician-rated PTSD severity assessed with the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 (CAPS-5) and self-reported symptoms assessed with the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5). Mechanistic assessments examined extinction recall using behavioral, psychophysiological, and neuroimaging measures. Across both drug conditions, clinician-rated and self-reported PTSD symptoms decreased substantially, and improvements were maintained through 3-month follow-up, at which point 91% of participants no longer met diagnostic criteria for PTSD. Significant improvements were also observed for anxiety, depression, sleep quality, and dissociative symptoms. The study was not powered to detect between-group differences; however, descriptive contrasts yielded numerically lower PTSD severity and reduced persistence of dissociative symptoms among THC-treated participants. THC was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events. During extinction recall, THC was associated with greater hippocampal differentiation between extinguished and unextinguished threat cues, whereas behavioral and psychophysiological measures did not differ between groups. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and tolerability of pairing low-dose THC with PE therapy and support evaluation in adequately powered randomized trials.

papers.title: Smaller Cortical Responses to Balance Perturbations in Parkinson's Disease with Freezing of Gait.
papers.abstract: Freezing of gait (FoG) is among the most disabling symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD) and is associated with balance impairment and increased falls risk, yet remains challenging to understand due to its episodic and context-dependent nature. Altered supplementary motor area (SMA) function at rest and before self-initiated movements has been implicated in FoG; however, whether this extends to functionally relevant balance behavior is unknown. A loss of balance in response to support surface translations during standing elicits a perturbation-evoked N1 potential, an error assessment signal linked to SMA activity. We therefore predicted that people with FoG would have smaller and later N1 responses than people with PD without FoG and older adults. We recorded electroencephalography (EEG) during backward support-surface translations in 29 people with PD (71 ± 7 years), including 13 people with a history of FoG (FoG+) and 16 people without FoG (FoG-), and 26 older adults (OA; 67 ± 6 years). N1 amplitude and latency were quantified at a central midline electrode and defined as the largest negative peak 100-300 ms post-perturbation. N1 responses were similar between OA and FoG-(Δ = 4.0 µV and 2.8 ms, respectively). In contrast, FoG+ had smaller N1 amplitudes than FoG- (Δ = 18.1 µV, p = 0.001) and OA (Δ = 14.1 µV, p = 0.003), and both differences persisted after adjusting for age. FoG+ also had later N1 latencies than OA (Δ = 26.5 ms, p = 0.029), with a similar but non-significant difference versus FoG- (Δ = 23.6 ms, p = 0.091); after adjusting for age, these latency differences were not retained. These findings suggest that perturbation-evoked cortical activity is altered in FoG, potentially reflecting altered SMA function, and may provide a functionally relevant marker of FoG susceptibility.

papers.title: Electric and Magnetic Source Imaging in Epilepsy: Anatomical Insights from Realistic Simulations.
papers.abstract: Neurosurgery is an effective treatment for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), but its success depends on the accurate delineation of the epileptogenic focus, approximated noninvasively by electric and magnetic source imaging (ESI/MSI) of high-density electroencephalography (HD-EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG). These modalities have distinct sensitivity profiles; consequently, epileptiform activity detected by one modality may remain undetected by the other. However, the implications of these differences for spike detectability and localization accuracy, and the added value of combined electromagnetic source imaging (EMSI), remain insufficiently characterized under clinically realistic conditions. Here, we characterize HD-EEG and MEG sensitivity profiles and compare ESI, MSI, and EMSI, using realistic simulations with known ground truth. We generated HD-EEG and MEG datasets from cortical, insular, and hippocampal sources across multiple orientations, activated using patient-derived intracranial EEG spike waveforms. Spike sensitivity and localization accuracy were evaluated using dipole scanning, dynamic statistical parametric mapping (dSPM), and linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV). EEG demonstrated higher spike detection rates and sensitivity for radially cortical sources at gyral crowns and sulcal bottoms ( p <0.001), while MEG detected more spikes from tangential cortical sources along sulcal walls ( p <0.001). MSI localized tangential sources more accurately than ESI across all methods ( p <0.001), while dipole scanning outperformed dSPM and LCMV for cortical and insular sources ( p <0.001). EMSI outperformed ESI ( p <0.001) but did not improve localization over MSI. These findings suggest that complementary anatomical sensitivities of HD-EEG and MEG may improve epileptogenic source characterization, supporting simultaneous acquisition during the presurgical evaluation of patients with DRE. EEG and MEG exhibit complementary sensitivity profiles, with EEG detecting more spikes from gyral crowns and sulcal bottoms and MEG from sulcal walls.MSI provides more focal and precise source localization than ESI, particularly for tangentially oriented sources.Dipole-based inverse method achieves higher localization accuracy than experimental dSPM and LCMV.

papers.title: Music-Synchronized Gamma Light Stimulation Strengthens Theta-Gamma Coupling in Older Adults with Cognitive Impairment: Results from a Randomized Feasibility Trial.
papers.abstract: Noninvasive clinical innovations for restoring gamma activity via sound and light stimulation have the potential to improve memory and cognitive abilities in Alzheimer's disease. We assessed whether pairing music with theta- and gamma-band light changes memory-supporting neural dynamics, and whether those changes track cognition. In an ongoing randomized feasibility trial, 38 older adults with cognitive impairment completed eight weeks of an audiovisual intervention. The treatment group (n = 19) listened to self-selected music while viewing light stimulation that consisted of a 39-Hz gamma-band signal modulated by delta- and theta-band musical rhythms. The control group (n = 19) listened to podcasts while viewing synchronized lights without the gamma frequency (delta-band only). Before and after the 8-week intervention, participants completed a face-name association task and the Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive (ADAS-Cog). Individuals in the treatment group showed significant improvements on a face-name association task and the ADAS-Cog. Cluster-based permutation testing showed a larger increase in phase-amplitude coupling between acoustic theta phase and frontal EEG gamma amplitude in the treatment group compared to the control group. Across participants, increases in stimulus-driven theta to EEG-gamma phase-amplitude coupling were associated with improvements in memory. These preliminary results suggest that theta-gamma stimulation delivered through music and lights strengthens cross-frequency coupling, and may correspondingly strengthen associative memory.

papers.title: Polydrug use and recreational motives are associated with lower posttraumatic symptoms in survivors of a mass trauma event.
papers.abstract: Drug use after trauma is common, but polydrug use patterns, motives, and associations with subsequent symptoms are poorly understood. We examined these associations among mass-casualty terror attack survivors, 72% of whom used drugs immediately before trauma exposure. Survivors of the October 7, 2023 Nova Festival attack reported use of six drug types (alcohol, cannabis, ketamine, stimulants, MDMA, psychedelics) and motives (avoidance, emotional regulation, self-medication, sleep, recreation) longitudinally at three timepoints (TP): 1-6 months (N=772), 8-12 months (N=453), and 17-24 months (N=302) post-attack. Separate latent class analyses of TP2 data characterized drug use, motives, and their combination. Linear regression and mixed-effects models examined associations between class membership and PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5) scores, adjusting for age, sex, time since trauma, and TP1 PCL-5 scores. At TP2, 70% reported polydrug use, 17% used one drug, and 13% reported no use. The high drug-load class (mean 4.6 drug types) had lower PCL-5 scores than the low drug-load class (mean 1.5 drug types); this difference was evident among participants using ≥4 drug types and persisted through TP3. The self-medication-motive class had higher PCL-5 scores than the recreational-motive class. In joint analyses, recreational-motive users at both low and high drug loads had lower PCL-5 scores than participants reporting self-medication motives and primarily cannabis use. Polydrug use was common among the mass-trauma survivors in our study. Self-medication motives were associated with higher PTSD symptom severity than recreational motives. Unexpectedly, higher polydrug use was associated with lower PTSD symptom scores.

papers.title: Time-of-Day-Dependent Effectiveness of Anti-IgE Therapy in Asthma: Clinical and Experimental Evidence.
papers.abstract: Asthma is a time-sensitive inflammatory disease whose activity exhibits daily (circadian) rhythms. An outstanding question is whether such temporal variations extend to advanced asthma treatments like biologics that are used for moderate-to-severe disease. To examine how time-of-administration relates to the effectiveness of the anti-IgE biologic, omalizumab. We performed a retrospective cohort study of omalizumab effectiveness in 153 patients with asthma with timestamped administration records. Time of day was modeled as a continuous variable and dichotomized into morning (8:00-11:59, n=74) versus afternoon (12:00-17:00, n=79) administration. Multivariable logistic regression and Cox time-to-event analyses were used to adjust for key covariates. For biological validation, we treated ovalbumin (OVA)-sensitized mice with anti-IgE antibody at various times of day and measured its impact on inflammatory lung pathology. Receiving the initial dose of omalizumab in the afternoon was associated with better response, defined as a 50% or more reduction in asthma exacerbations in the year after initiation (Odds ratio, OR: 5.20; 95% CI, 1.94-13.96). For each hour later in the day the initial dose of omalizumab was given, the odds of a response increased by 34% (adjusted OR, 1.34; 1.02-1.77). In OVA-sensitized mice, anti-IgE treatment attenuated inflammatory lung pathology, including OVA-induced airway hyperresponsiveness and type-2 inflammation-related gene expression, in a time-of-day-sensitive manner, with maximum effectiveness when dosed in the latter part of the dark phase, functionally analogous to the afternoon in humans. The timing of anti-IgE treatment for asthma may influence therapeutic success. These findings have implications for optimizing the effectiveness of respiratory biologics. IgE-targeted therapy in patients with asthma and in murine experimental asthma varied in effectiveness based on administration time.In patients, receiving the first omalizumab dose in the PM (vs. AM) was associated with better treatment response.

papers.title: Study protocol for evidence-based LIFEstyle interventions for the delay of COgnitive DEcline among Singaporean older adults (LIFECODES): a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Singapore's rapidly aging population has led to a widening gap between total and healthy life expectancy. Dementia affects approximately 10% of adults aged ≥ 60 years, and 152,000 people are projected to be living with dementia by 2030. Up to 45% of dementia cases may theoretically be prevented or delayed by addressing 14 modifiable risk factors across the life course. However, evidence on clinically effective, culturally tailored multidomain interventions for older Singaporeans remains limited. The LIFEstyle interventions for the delay of COgnitive DEcline among older Singaporean adults (LIFECODES) trial evaluates the effects of a multidomain lifestyle intervention on cognitive decline and the added value of individualized health coaching. Secondary aims examine epigenetic aging and systemic inflammation. LIFECODES is a three-arm proof-of-concept randomized controlled trial at the National University of Singapore (NUS) aiming to enroll 120 community-dwelling adults aged 60-75 years with signs of cognitive decline. Participants are randomized to group-based health education (GHE), GHE plus individualized health coaching (HC), or general care. The two-year intervention comprises 27 in-person sessions addressing eight lifestyle domains relevant to dementia risk: diet, physical activity, cognitive activity, social engagement, mental well-being, sleep, smoking and alcohol consumption. The primary outcome is cognitive processing speed. Secondary outcomes include memory, executive function and other cognitive domains, DNA methylation (DNAm) age, inflammatory biomarkers, functional status, psychosocial well-being, and sleep quality. As of 14 September 2026, 190 individuals had been screened, and 110 (57.9%) met the eligibility criteria. Seven eligible individuals withdrew before randomization and 12 withdrew after randomization. A total of 91 participants are currently enrolled in the study (GHE, n = 30; HC, n = 30; control, n = 31). The first rolling intervention cohort began on 15 May 2025. Among the 91 participants, the mean age is 68.7 years (SD 4.2), and 66 (72.5%) are female. Recruitment and follow-up remain ongoing. Interim recruitment and randomization indicate that a community-based multidomain dementia-prevention trial can be initiated in Singapore. Planned analyses will determine intervention efficacy and the added value of individualized health coaching for cognitive health and biological aging. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06661486, identifier NCT06661486.

papers.title: Associations Between Cannabis Use and Sleep Outcomes in a Sample of Pregnant Women.
papers.abstract: Both sleep difficulties and cannabis use during pregnancy (CUP) are common and associated with adverse birth and offspring outcomes. Sleep problems are a commonly reported motive for cannabis use during pregnancy. Estimate associations between cannabis use during pregnancy and common sleep difficulties across trimesters. This cohort study recruited pregnant women with lifetime cannabis use who used (n=298) and did not use (n=143) cannabis during pregnancy. Women who reported heavy episodic alcohol consumption or use of other illicit substances were excluded. Some women tested positive for cotinine in urine drug screens. Cannabis use was assessed at each trimester using self-report and urine drug screening. Presence of the nicotine metabolite, cotinine, was measured via urine drug screening at each trimester. Cannabis use during pregnancy (CUP) status was defined separately for each trimester as use versus no use and was treated as a time-varying exposure. The nicotine metabolite cotinine was included as a covariate in all models to account for nicotine exposure. Motivation for cannabis use during pregnancy was assessed during the first trimester. Insomnia symptoms (Women's Health Initiative Insomnia Rating Scale), daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale), subjective sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index single item), and restless legs symptoms were assessed at each trimester. A CUP Status x Trimester interaction was observed for insomnia symptoms (F(2,737.81)=4.98, P FDR =0.03) wherein use during the third trimester was associated with heightened insomnia. Women reporting sleep difficulties as a motive for use reported worse insomnia symptoms (F(1, 223)=13.09, P FDR =0.001) and worse sleep quality (F(1, 219)=7.86, P FDR =0.01), relative to those using for other reasons. Elevated third trimester insomnia symptoms among pregnant women using cannabis compared to women who did not use cannabis suggest a potential trimester-sensitive association. Despite perceptions that cannabis improves sleep, women who reported sleep as their motive for CUP during the first trimester experienced greater insomnia symptoms and poorer sleep quality across pregnancy than those using cannabis for other reasons. Additional studies are needed to determine whether sleep-related difficulties precede cannabis use, follow it, are modified by it, or represent an epiphenomenon. Question: Is cannabis use during pregnancy associated with maternal sleep problems?Findings: Within this study of 441 pregnant women, cannabis use was associated with higher third trimester insomnia symptoms but not with other sleep outcomes. Women using cannabis to aid with sleep difficulties had worse insomnia symptoms and poorer sleep quality than those using for other reasons.Meaning: Cannabis use in late pregnancy may mark periods of greater insomnia symptom burden, suggesting that sleep problems during pregnancy may be an important clinical context for understanding cannabis use during pregnancy.

papers.title: Tyrosine hydroxylase deletion in Ntsr1 neurons confers resistance to diet-induced weight gain: an energy-balance analysis.
papers.abstract: High-fat diet (HFD) disrupts circadian feeding rhythms and promotes diet-induced obesity (DIO), but the neural mechanisms linking diet to energy balance remain unclear. Previously, we demonstrated that dopamine production in neurotensin receptor 1 ( Ntsr1 )-expressing neurons was required for HFD-induced daytime overfeeding and DIO. Here, we tested whether DIO resistance in Ntsr1 Cre ;Th flox conditional knockout (cKO) mice was explained by altered energy expenditure. We replicated resistance to HFD-induced weight gain and assessed food intake, indirect calorimetry, activity, body temperature, fecal energy, fecal nonesterified fatty acids, and the gut microbiome. Indirect calorimetry on standard chow diet (SCD) was confounded by reduced intake and body weight loss, whereas HFD-fed cKO mice consumed food readily and resisted weight gain. Unlike our previous study, daytime feeding was not suppressed; instead, cKO mice were slightly and variably hypophagic on HFD but not SCD. DIO resistance was not accompanied by increased energy expenditure, activity, or body temperature. Rather, cKO mice showed reduced energy expenditure and activity and lower body temperature on both diets. In the replication cohort, HFD fecal output was lower in cKO mice, whereas the independent bomb-calorimetry cohort showed no genotype difference in fecal mass; fecal energy density and nonesterified fatty acid concentration were unchanged. Preliminary analysis of the microbiome was consistent with an obesity-resistant gut profile. Together, these findings indicate that the feeding phenotype is diet- and experiment-dependent and that DIO resistance is not explained by increased energy expenditure, activity, thermogenesis, or detectable changes in fecal energy or fat content.

papers.title: Hypoxic Burden Predicts Symptomatic but Not Sleep Architecture Response to CPAP Therapy in Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.abstract: The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) remains the standard metric for assessing obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, although it does not fully capture the physiological consequences of respiratory events. Hypoxic burden (HB), which integrates the frequency, depth, and duration of oxygen desaturations, has been proposed as a more comprehensive measure of OSA-related hypoxic stress. This study compared the prognostic value of HB and AHI for subjective and objective treatment outcomes in patients undergoing continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. Data from 412 patients with OSA who underwent diagnostic and CPAP-treated polysomnography were analyzed, including 52 patients with available follow-up questionnaires. HB was calculated using a validated event-based algorithm. Multivariable regression models were used to predict patient-reported outcomes and changes in sleep architecture, adjusted for age, sex and body mass index. HB consistently demonstrated stronger associations with symptomatic outcomes than AHI. Models including HB showed improved model fit and explained variance. HB remained independently associated with lower follow-up fatigue and better sleep quality after adjustment for AHI. In contrast, AHI was the dominant predictor of objective sleep architecture improvements, including increases in N3 sleep, reductions in N1 sleep, and reductions in arousal index. HB provided additional independent information only for changes in arousal burden. These findings suggest that HB and AHI capture complementary dimensions of OSA severity. While AHI primarily reflects sleep fragmentation and physiological response to CPAP, HB appears more closely related to subjective treatment benefit. Incorporating HB alongside AHI may improve clinical phenotyping and prediction of treatment response in OSA.

papers.title: Early Increases in Hippocampal Synchrony Predict Chronic Epileptiform Burden in a Temporal Lobe Epilepsy Model.
papers.abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE), the most common focal epilepsy, is often drug-resistant and arises predominantly in the hippocampus. Disease severity is conventionally assessed by seizure frequency and duration, yet epileptiform activity outside discrete seizures may also track disease progression. Whether this activity reflects hippocampal network reorganization as part of epileptogenesis, and whether such reorganization predicts chronic severity, is unknown. Here, we combined longitudinal two-photon calcium imaging of hippocampal CA1 neurons with repeated 24-hour EEG recordings that quantified epileptiform burden in the same pilocarpine-treated mice over 16 weeks. CA1 firing and synchrony rose acutely, subsided during a latent period, and increased again chronically, with synchronized firing organized into brief waves that propagated in a consistent direction. Epileptiform burden followed a similar temporal trajectory and increasingly contained electrographic seizures. CA1 synchrony correlated with epileptiform burden and stratified mice into groups with distinct neuronal and electrographic outcomes. CA1 synchrony measured within three weeks of pilocarpine induction predicted chronic epileptiform burden, identifying early hippocampal synchrony as a candidate imaging biomarker and pointing to an early window for intervention in TLE.

papers.title: Enhancing psychological wellbeing in STEM education through public health strategies across educational transitions.
papers.abstract: Student mental health is a growing public health concern in higher education, and small questionnaire datasets are often highly imbalanced and difficult to model reliably. This study empirically validates a Transition-Aware Public Health Wellbeing Network (TAPHW-Net) using an openly accessible questionnaire dataset and narrows the STEM-transition domain to the available variables. The source dataset contained 843 responses. Respondents aged 18-22 years were retained, and the analytic sample consisted of 777 students, classified based on the original survey label: No Stress (n = 38), Eustress (n = 710), and Distress (n = 29). 24 predictors were grouped into emotional/psychological, physical/somatic, academic pressure, social and environmental, and demographic branches. To prevent leakage of the targets, the direct recent-stress item was omitted. Median imputation, standardization, and SMOTE were applied in the training folds only. Five-fold out-of-fold evaluation was used to assess Logistic Regression, SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, MLP, ANN, and TAPHW-Net. Logistic Regression had the highest fold-averaged accuracy (0.968 ± 0.019), macro-F1 (0.884 ± 0.048), and macro-AUC (0.996 ± 0.004). TAPHW-Net's pooled OOF accuracy, macro-F1 score, and macro-AUC were 0.8739, 0.6626, and 0.9523, respectively. It had lower overall accuracy, but it successfully retrieved 78.9% of the No Stress cases and 86.2% of the distress cases, although precision was only 0.385 and 0.397 for these two classes, respectively. Difficulty in the home environment, anxiety, palpitations, work-environment stress, sleep problems, and health problems were important predictors. The attention architecture did not outperform simpler models on this small and highly imbalanced tabular dataset. Its main value lies in domain-structured representations, minority-class recall, and transparent mapping of model importance to a hypothetical decision-support template. The findings are limited to the source dataset and require external validation before institutional use or transfer to STEM-specific and educational-transition settings.

papers.title: Norepinephrine inhibits Afferent activation of NTS Catecholamine Neurons in Mice.
papers.abstract: The nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS) integrates visceral sensory input to regulate feeding behavior, with catecholaminergic (CA) and neuropeptide Y (NPY)-expressing neurons playing key roles in energy homeostasis. Recent evidence suggests functional heterogeneity among CA-NTS neurons, including distinct subpopulations that either suppress or promote feeding. In this study, we investigated how norepinephrine (NE) modulates excitatory synaptic transmission from solitary tract (ST) afferents onto tyrosine hydroxylase-positive (TH⁺) NTS neurons in mice. Using patch-clamp electrophysiology in horizontal brainstem slices, we found that NE inhibits ST-evoked excitatory postsynaptic currents (ST-EPSCs) in a concentration-dependent manner, with maximal effects at ≥10 µM and an EC₅₀ of ∼3.4 µM. This inhibition was mediated by α₂-adrenergic receptors and was independent of GABA A receptor activity. NE also suppressed asynchronous glutamate release and attenuated CCK-induced increase in spontaneous EPSC frequency, suggesting a presynaptic mechanism. NPY similarly reduced ST-EPSC amplitude via Y 2 receptor activation, and co-application of NE and NPY produce additive or synergistic effects, even at subthreshold concentrations. Together, our results reveal a novel mechanism by which noradrenergic and peptidergic systems interact to regulate visceral sensory processing in the brainstem. NTS.

papers.title: Circadian feeding rhythm loss drives sex-specific β-cell dysfunction in diet-induced obesity.
papers.abstract: Diet-induced obesity (DIO), modeled by a high-fat diet (HFD), adversely affects circadian glucose homeostasis partly by dysregulating fasting/feeding cycles. However, its impact on circadian β-cell function and relevant transcriptional programs remains unclear. To investigate this, we exposed male and female C57BL/6 mice to either chow or HFD for eight weeks and assessed behavioral (feeding/activity), physiological (glucose tolerance/insulin secretion), transcriptomic (RNA sequencing (RNA-seq)), and epigenomic (Assay for Transposase-Accessible Chromatin using Sequencing (ATAC-seq)) circadian rhythms. Additionally, we tested whether normalizing fasting/feeding cycles via time-restricted feeding (tRF) during the dark- or light-phase of the circadian cycle could mitigate DIO's deleterious effects. DIO disrupted circadian fasting/feeding rhythms, with greater disruption in males than females (p<0.05 vs. CHOW). In males, DIO abolished circadian regulation of glucose tolerance and in vivo glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) (p<0.05 vs. chow), whereas female mice maintained circadian glucose homeostasis. RNA-seq analysis of male islets revealed a 42.1% reduction in circadian-regulated transcripts under DIO, with weakened rhythms in key β-cell pathways such as insulin secretion. Moreover, ATAC-Seq analysis indicated reduced chromatin accessibility of genes/pathways related to insulin secretion and glucose hemostasis under DIO (p<0.05 vs. chow) during both dark- or light-phase of the circadian cycle. Notably, dark-phase time-restricted feeding (tRF) restored circadian glucose tolerance, GSIS, and islet gene expression, whereas light-phase tRF enhanced β-cell function during the normally inactive/light phase of the circadian cycle, further suppressing circadian rhythmicity of the islet transcriptome. Motif analysis indicated that DIO suppressed the activity of D-box transcription factors (TFs) (DBP and TEF) while enhancing the activity of ETS family TFs (ELK1, ETS2, ELF2, and GABPA), which was partly mitigated by dark-phase tRF. Our study demonstrates that DIO disrupts circadian β-cell function and gene expression by dysregulating fasting/feeding cycles in male mice and reveals significant sex differences in how DIO affects circadian glucose homeostasis and β-cell function.

papers.title: The relationship between Tai Chi exercise and psychological distress in older adults: the chain mediation effect of mood state and sleep quality.
papers.abstract: Psychological distress is a common mental health issue among older adults, significantly affecting their quality of life and overall health. As a traditional form of mind-body exercise, Tai Chi is gaining increasing attention for its mental health benefits. However, the effects of Tai Chi practice on psychological distress in older adults remain unclear, and the mechanisms underlying its impact on mood and sleep quality, in particular, still need to be explored. This study aims to explore the relationship between Tai Chi exercise and psychological distress in older adults, and to examine the chained mediating effects of mood state and sleep quality in this association. Questionnaires containing the Physical Activity Rating Scale (PARS-3), the Positive and Negative Mood States (POMS) scale, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQ), and the final versions of non-specific psychological distress scales (Kessler 10), a total of 457 valid questionnaires were collected. Analysis of the mediation effects in this study were statistically consistent with a mediating role of the relationship between Tai Chi exercise and psychological distress in older adults. The effect size of the total indirect effect was -0.265 (95% CI [-0.339, -0.197], p < 0.01), accounting for 53.9% of the total effect. The mediation effect consisted of three pathways. Path 1: Tai Chi exercise → Mood state → Psychological distress in older adults, with an effect size of -0.159 (95% CI [-0.221, -0.103], p < 0.01). Path 2: Tai Chi exercise → Sleep quality → Psychological distress in older adults, with an effect size of -0.067 (95% CI [-0.112, -0.032], p < 0.01). Path 3: Tai Chi exercise → Mood state → Sleep quality → Psychological distress in older adults, with an effect size of -0.039 (95% CI [-0.065, -0.020], p < 0.01). This study identified a significant association between Tai Chi exercise and the alleviation of psychological distress in older adults, and this association may be explained by the chained mediating effects of mood state and sleep quality.

papers.title: Partial agonists and heteromeric Kainate receptor desensitization.
papers.abstract: Kainate receptors (KARs) are glutamate-gated ion channels that mediate fast excitatory synaptic transmission in the central nervous system. KARs assemble as homo- or heterotetramers composed of five subunits (GluK1-5), with heteromeric assemblies representing the predominant native population. Although KARs share overall structures and basic functional properties with other ionotropic glutamate receptor subfamilies, they exhibit distinct gating kinetics, particularly with respect to desensitization. While earlier studies have demonstrated how agonist binding drives gate opening and subsequent desensitization, the mechanisms governing partial agonism and desensitization of KARs, especially in heteromeric KARs, remain incompletely understood. Here, we combine electrophysiology and microscale thermophoresis binding assays to investigate how distinct KAR partial agonists control KAR desensitization and its recovery. While the onset rates of desensitization of homo- and heteromeric receptors activated by high/saturating concentrations of partial agonists are conserved between GluK2 and GluK2/GluK5 receptors, recovery from desensitization in heteromers is significantly slower than in homomers. Together with structural modeling and analysis of the GluK2 and GluK5 ligand binding domains (LBDs) in complex with orthosteric ligands, we show that agonist residence time and the extent of LBD bi-lobe closure across various agonists take precedence over subunit composition in governing KAR desensitization.

papers.title: Human herpesvirus 7-associated encephalitis diagnosed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing in pediatric patients: a retrospective study.
papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to describe the clinical features, treatment and prognosis of immunocompetent children with human herpes virus 7 (HHV-7)-associated encephalitis. Sixteen children with HHV-7-associated encephalitis were diagnosed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing of their cerebrospinal fluid and followed up for 3 months. The median age of the cohort was 8.6 years (range, 1.4-11.8) and comprised of 8 males and 8 females. The most common presenting symptoms were fever (12/16, 75.0%), headache (10/16, 62.5%), and vomiting (8/16, 50.0%). Abnormal electroencephalography and encephalitis-related neuroimaging findings were obtained in 50.0% (6/12) and 25.0% (4/16) of the patients, respectively. 68.8% of the patients were treated with either acyclovir or ganciclovir. Unfavorable outcomes occurred in three patients, including the death of a 2-year-old child. Pediatric HHV-7-associated encephalitis generally has a favorable prognosis, but severe cases do occur. Early recognition is important for increasing clinicians' awareness of this condition.

papers.title: Intrinsic timekeeping in Escherichia coli.
papers.abstract: Circadian clocks allow organisms to anticipate predictable environmental changes across the day-night cycle. Here we show that the bacterium Escherichia coli exhibits intrinsic timekeeping that anticipates daily temperature cycles. E. coli biofilms entrained to daily temperature shifts, producing 24-hour rhythms in curli plaque formation that persisted under constant temperature. Mechanistically, genetic analyses localized the autonomous timing machinery to the Rcs phosphorelay, which exhibits structural and conceptual parallels with other circadian systems. The BluFR sensory pathway, which acts upstream of the Rcs phosphorelay, linked temperature and blue-light cycles to rhythmic curli production. Flagellar promoter activity and curli production peaked at opposite times of day, suggesting daily coordination of adhesion and motility programs. These findings identify an intrinsic timing system in E. coli that expands our understanding of biological timekeeping.

papers.title: Practice patterns of midazolam administration in patients undergoing cardiac-related non-operating room procedures: analysis of a US anaesthesia database.
papers.abstract: Midazolam can be administered as an anxiolytic, a cardio-stable sedative, or an anaesthetic agent during non-operating room anaesthesia (NORA) procedures. Guidelines suggest avoidance in older or frail patients, and current practices are unknown. We hypothesised that there would be significant variation in midazolam administration for cardiac-related NORA procedures by attending and institutional characteristics, in addition to patient characteristics. This is a retrospective observational analysis of a multi-institution US-centric electronic health record dataset including all adult patients undergoing cardiac-related NORA procedures in the Multicenter Perioperative Outcomes Group database from 2015 to 2022. The primary aim of the study was to identify the proportion of total variance in midazolam administration attributable to patient-, attending-, and institutional-level factors. The secondary aim was to identify practice pattern variations in the dosage and timing of midazolam administration. The primary outcome was any midazolam administration ≤1 h before anaesthesia start to 1 h after anaesthesia end. Secondary outcomes included total dose and timing of midazolam administration. Variance in midazolam administration attributable to patient, attending, and institutional factors was calculated with intraclass correlation coefficients following multilevel mixed-effects generalised linear models, in which a three-level nesting structure was assumed: patients nested within attendings and attendings nested within institutions. For the primary outcome, a binomial distribution and logit link function was specified. For the secondary outcome of total midazolam, the same three-level nesting structure was used, and covariates were modelled using a multilevel mixed-effects model specifying a Gaussian distribution and identity link function. A total of 246 918 cardiac-related NORA procedures with care provided by 5212 unique anaesthesia attendings across 63 institutions with a median case volume of 9 (inter-quartile range [IQR] 2-37) were included in the analysis. Midazolam was administered in 33.0% of patients (n=81 602), including 25.5% of patients aged ≥65 yr (n=40 469). Midazolam administration declined from 50.7% of patients in 2015 to 29.0% in 2022 (P<0.001). The median dose was 2 mg (IQR 2-2), with 89.9% administered before procedure start. For transoesophageal echocardiography procedures, it was estimated that 37.0% of midazolam administration (30.4-44.3) was attributable to attending variation and 26.4% (19.2-35.2) to the institution, assuming that 36.6% of the variation was attributable to known patient factors. For transcatheter/endovascular procedures, attending, institution, and patient factors accounted for 45.7% (39.0-52.6), 27.7% (19.7-37.4), and 26.6%, respectively. Although patient-level factors accounted for a meaningful proportion of variability, substantial variation in midazolam administration was also attributable to attending- and institution-level factors. Further studies on clinical outcomes and patient experience associated with this type of midazolam administration have the potential to inform future practice.
