Most participants (28/36; 78%) who started the study medication were able to titrate up to the maximum daily dose of 2.5 mL (125 mg CBD/5 mg THC). Of the 37 participants randomized, 30 (81%) completed their 26-week follow-up visit. Participants' mean age was 66 (standard deviation [SD] 9.4), most were female (76%) and had never used cannabis (81%). At the 12-week follow-up, 41% in the placebo arm (7 of 17) reported moderate-to-severe CPSP, and 13% in the MPL-001 arm (2 of 15). At 26-weeks follow-up, 19% in the placebo arm (3 of 16) reported moderate-to-severe CPSP, and 14% in the MPL-001 arm (2 of 14). One patient in the treatment arm that reported CPSP at both follow-up times did not take any study medication. There were 18 treatment-related adverse events reported among 11 patients randomized to MPL-001, and 19 treatment-related adverse events reported among 12 patients randomized to placebo. The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal, typically nausea and diarrhea. Modifications to our study protocol will be required to ensure feasibility of a definitive trial of cannabis versus placebo to reduce CPSP among TKA patients. For the definitive trial, we will expand participant recruitment to additional centres and switch from oil drops to capsules to increase adherence. Clinicaltrials.gov NCT03825965.

papers.title: A comparative study of network structures between different sedentary behaviors and depressive symptoms in adolescents with and without non-suicidal self-injury.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to examine association networks between sedentary behaviors and depressive symptoms among adolescents with and without non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI), compare network structures and global connectivity between the two groups, and identify key bridge nodes within each network. A total of 8,102 Chinese adolescents were included, comprising 1,996 in the NSSI group and 6,106 in the Non-NSSI group. Nine types of sedentary behaviors and 20 depressive symptoms from the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D) were assessed using self-reported questionnaires. Based on a mixed correlation matrix, sedentary behavior-depressive symptom networks were estimated separately for the two groups using the extended Bayesian information criterion graphical LASSO (EBICglasso), and bridge strength and one-step bridge expected influence were computed. A network comparison test was conducted to compare network structure and global strength between groups, along with covariate-adjusted sensitivity analyses. Significant differences in network structure were observed between the two groups (M = 0.114, P < 0.001), indicating distinct conditional association patterns between sedentary behaviors and depressive symptoms in adolescents with and without NSSI. The global strength was 11.913 for the NSSI group and 11.476 for the Non-NSSI group, with a non-significant difference of 0.437 (3.8%, P = 0.636). In the NSSI group, mobile phone/tablet use, offline classes/tutoring, and sitting and chatting showed higher bridge expected influence, while difficulty concentrating, reduced speech, and restless sleep emerged as prominent bridge symptom nodes. After covariate adjustment, the network structure differences remained statistically significant, whereas differences in global strength remained non-significant; core bridge nodes were largely preserved in both groups. Although differences were observed in the specific association structures of sedentary behavior-depressive symptom networks between adolescents with and without NSSI, there was no evidence that the NSSI group exhibited significantly higher overall network connectivity. Mobile phone/tablet use, study-related sedentary behaviors, sitting and chatting, and symptoms related to attention, sleep, and social withdrawal may represent important candidate nodes for future longitudinal studies and risk screening; however, their causal roles and potential intervention value require further investigation.

papers.title: Happy Homework 2.0: effects on 24-hour movement behaviours in children-findings from a pilot cluster randomised controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Children's 24-h movement behaviours-physical activity, sedentary behaviour, and sleep-are critical to health and wellbeing, yet many fail to meet recommended daily guidelines. School-based health interventions offer a scalable approach to improve movement behaviours, though their impact may be limited by competing academic demands. Homework presents an opportunity to extend the reach of school-based health interventions into the home environment. Happy Homework (HH 2.0) was developed as a digital intervention to integrate movement-based activities into home routines. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and usability of HH 2.0 among primary school children. An 8-week pilot cluster randomised controlled trial was conducted across four primary schools in the West of Scotland, with classes randomly allocated to intervention or control. Feasibility, usability, and acceptability were assessed using basic app-usage analytics and questionnaires completed by children, parents and teachers. Secondary outcomes included physical activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep measured via activPAL devices, which provided multiple posture- and movement-based metrics. Self-report sleep questionnaires were included, with children's motivation measured through basic psychological need satisfaction questionnaires. Linear mixed-effects models examined group by time interactions, accounting for clustering by school and repeated measures. A total of 82 children aged 8-12 years were recruited (60% of those invited), with 87% retained at follow up, indicating good feasibility. App-use analytics indicated repeated engagement, although overall use was modest, defined by declining frequency and duration of interactions over time. Secondary outcome data from activPAL devices demonstrated a significant group x time difference in sedentary behaviour, with greater increases in the intervention group compared to the control (B = 66.2 min/day, p < .05). Self-reported sleep also showed a significant group × time interaction, with smaller increases in reported sleep duration in the intervention group relative to control (p < .01). No other significant group × time interactions were found for other secondary outcomes. HH 2.0 was feasible and acceptable as a homework-based health intervention however, engagement levels likely limited its effectiveness. Findings outline the potential and challenges of digital school-based health interventions and emphasises the need to strengthen implementation strategies, sustain engagement, and enhance parent and teacher involvement. NCT07631754 (retrospectively registered).
papers.journal: Journal of activity, sedentary and sleep behaviors

papers.title: Screen use, lifestyle habits and mental health in preschool children: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Excessive screen exposure is associated with sleep disturbances, unhealthy dietary patterns, reduced physical activity, and poorer socio-emotional wellbeing. This study aimed to: (1) assess the association between screen time and lifestyle habits, and (2) examine the associations of screen time and lifestyle habits with emotional and behavioral difficulties in preschool children. This cross-sectional study included 931 children (2-6 years) from Portugal. Parents completed questionnaires on children's lifestyle habits and emotional and behavioral difficulties using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ). Anthropometric measurements were collected. Screen time was classified as low (≤ 60 min/day), moderate (> 60 to < 120 min/day), or high (≥ 120 min/day). Linear and logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and parental education were performed. Regarding lifestyle habits, high screen time was associated with shorter weekday sleep duration and higher consumption of ultra-processed foods. No significant associations were observed with active play time or participation in extracurricular sports after adjustment. Regarding mental health, children with high screen time had higher odds of abnormal SDQ scores, indicating greater emotional and behavioral difficulties. Longer weekend sleep duration and lower maternal educational level were independently associated with SDQ categories. Higher screen time was associated with shorter weekday sleep duration, higher consumption of ultra-processed foods, and greater emotional and behavioral difficulties in preschool children. These findings support current recommendations promoting balanced screen use and healthy lifestyle habits during early childhood while highlighting the importance of family and sociodemographic factors for children's mental health.
papers.journal: Child and adolescent psychiatry and mental health

papers.title: Nsun5 deficiency leads to impaired myelin integrity and sleep disruption.
papers.abstract: Sleep disruption is common in disorders involving white-matter abnormalities, but the molecular pathways linking ribosomal RNA modification to disordered sleep remain unclear. NSUN5, which encodes an rRNA methyltransferase, is deleted in most patients with Williams-Beuren syndrome (WBS), a condition frequently accompanied by sleep problems. This clinical association suggests that loss of NSUN5 may contribute to sleep dysfunction, potentially through mechanisms relevant to white-matter integrity and neural activity. We combined electroencephalography/electromyography phenotyping, transcriptomics, ribosome profiling, nascent proteomics, proteomics, electron microscopy, positron emission tomography-computed tomography, and pharmacological rescue experiments in Nsun5-knockout mice to define how loss of Nsun5-dependent 28 S ribosomal RNA 5-methylcytosine affects white-matter integrity and sleep. Nsun5 deficiency markedly reduced 28 S rRNA m5C levels and led to selective translational dysregulation rather than global translational failure. The affected translational programs were enriched in myelination-related pathways and voltage-gated potassium channel subunits, including Kcna1 and Kcna2. At the cellular and tissue levels, these alterations were associated with oligodendrocyte loss, diffuse hypomyelination of the corpus callosum, and increased regional cortical metabolic activity. Correspondingly, Nsun5-knockout mice exhibited reduced non-rapid-eye-movement sleep and altered nocturnal sleep organization. Treatment with clemastine significantly improved sleep abnormalities and restored myelin integrity, while treatment with 4-aminopyridine also alleviated the sleep phenotype. These findings suggest that Nsun5-dependent rRNA methylation contributes to sleep disruption in association with white-matter dysfunction and altered potassium-channel-related protein abundance. Our results provide a preclinical framework for understanding sleep disturbances associated with WBS and other myelin-related neurological conditions.

papers.title: Upper airway dilator muscle dysfunction in obesity: role of the ATF5-LONP1 axis in lipotoxic stress and exercise-associated functional recovery.
papers.abstract: Obesity-related lipotoxic stress is associated with upper-airway dilator muscle dysfunction, yet endogenous stress responses governing mitochondrial quality control remain poorly defined. We investigated activating transcription factor 5 (ATF5)-Lon peptidase 1 (LONP1) signaling in mitochondrial quality control under lipotoxic stress, as well as its association with exercise-associated functional recovery. Clinical data from 1,546 adults were analyzed using multivariable models and propensity score-matched sensitivity analyses. Palatopharyngeal muscle specimens from 10 participants with obesity and 10 normal-weight controls were examined. Diet-induced obesity (DIO) mice underwent sternohyoid contractility and plethysmography testing; a 12-week swimming group was compared with sedentary DIO and dietary-reversal (DIO-DR) groups. Palmitic acid-treated C2C12 myotubes were used for mechanistic studies, combining ATF5 and LONP1 gain- and loss-of-function approaches, mitochondrial assays, chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, promoter assays, and autophagic-flux analysis. Obesity was associated with elevated circulating creatine kinase (CK) and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH). Greater metabolic burden was independently associated with higher CK, LDH, and myoglobin, but not with high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) or creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB). Palatopharyngeal muscle from participants with obesity showed altered myofiber morphology and reduced myosin heavy chain (MyHC) immunoreactivity. DIO sternohyoid muscle exhibited lipid accumulation, mitochondrial abnormalities, and contractile dysfunction. In C2C12 myotubes, lipotoxic stress promoted nuclear ATF5 accumulation and occupancy at a conserved basic leucine zipper (bZIP) motif in the Lonp1 promoter. ATF5 overexpression improved mitochondrial respiration, redox-calcium homeostasis, and MyHC expression, whereas LONP1 knockdown attenuated these effects, and LONP1 overexpression partially reproduced this protective phenotype. Despite comparable final body weight and metabolic profiles between dietary-reversal and swimming-exercised groups, swimming produced greater improvements in sternohyoid force, inspiratory flow, and oxidative capacity, accompanied by enhanced ATF5-LONP1-associated mitochondrial stress-response markers. The findings support the ATF5-LONP1 axis as part of an adaptive mitochondrial stress response that contributes to exercise-associated recovery from obesity-related upper-airway muscle dysfunction. Mitochondrial quality control may represent a candidate translational target for obesity-related obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Not applicable.

papers.title: Longitudinal lifestyle changes and subsequent risks of depression and anxiety: a prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: The extent to which overall lifestyle changes over time affect subsequent risk of depression and anxiety remains unclear. We examined the associations of lifestyle deterioration, maintenance, and improvement with incident depression and anxiety. This prospective population-based cohort study included 18,678 UK Biobank participants free of depression and anxiety who completed lifestyle assessments at baseline (2006-10) and at a repeat assessment (2012-13). A healthy lifestyle score (HLS, range 0-7) was derived from smoking, alcohol consumption, diet, body mass index, physical activity, sleep, and sedentary behavior. Lifestyle change was assessed using differences in HLS between assessments. Joint lifestyle change patterns were created by baseline lifestyle profiles and subsequent changes. Independent of baseline lifestyle status, lifestyle deterioration was associated with increased risk of depression (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.20-1.67) and anxiety (HR 1.26, 95% CI 1.06-1.50). Each additional healthy lifestyle factor adopted over time was associated with an 18% lower risk of depression (HR, 0.82, 95% CI 0.76-0.88) and a 7% lower risk of anxiety (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.86-1.00). Participants maintaining poor lifestyle patterns (0-3 healthy lifestyle factors) experienced 2.86-fold and 1.72-fold higher risk of depression and anxiety, respectively, than those maintained an ideal lifestyle pattern (6-7 healthy factors). Lifestyle deterioration was associated with increased risk of depression and anxiety, whereas lifestyle improvement was associated with lower risk of both outcomes, highlighting maintaining and promoting healthier lifestyle for the prevention of depression and anxiety.
papers.journal: The international journal of behavioral nutrition and physical activity

papers.title: Brain somatic chromosome 1q gain causes focal cortical malformations and epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Brain somatic mutations are a major cause of epileptogenic focal cortical malformations. Hyaline astrocytic inclusions represent a rare neuropathological finding in epilepsy. We analyzed eight patients undergoing surgery for drug-resistant focal epilepsy associated with astrocytic inclusions, combining bulk and single-nucleus genomic analyses, cell-type-specific genetic profiling, neuropathological characterization, and electrophysiological recordings to establish genotype-neuropathology correlations. Microelectrode array recordings from cortical slices from one patient revealed spontaneous abnormal network activity in regions without astrocytic inclusions. Multilayered genomic analysis of surgical brain tissue, including single-nucleus sequencing, identified mosaic chromosome 1q copy-number gains in all eight cases, with chr1q tetrasomies confirmed in six. In four cases, the supernumerary chromosome 1q was of maternal origin, and long-read haplotyping in a patient-parent trio supported a novel mechanism of meiosis II chromosome missegregation. Chr1q gains were enriched in inclusion-bearing astrocytes, linking chromosomal aneuploidy to neuropathology. Finally, we developed a targeted sequencing panel enabling the detection of chr1q gains in surgical brain samples, including samples obtained from presurgical stereo-EEG electrodes. Together, these findings support postzygotic rescue of a maternal meiotic error in non-neural lineages as a mechanism of pathogenic brain mosaicism and define mosaic chr1q gain as a distinct cause of epilepsy.

papers.title: Efficacy and mechanisms of device-monitored aerobic exercise for depression treatment and cognitive function improvement (DAECD trail): protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Depression is a major public health concern, yet many patients fail to achieve remission with standard pharmacotherapy or psychotherapy, and often experience relapse and persistent cognitive impairments. Enhancing treatment outcome is therefore an urgent clinical need and aerobic exercise may have great potential. However, its efficacy in depression treatment and improving cognition, as well as the underlying mechanisms remains unclear. This device-monitored aerobic exercise for depression and cognition improvement (DAECD) trail will enroll 80 patients with depression, randomly assigned (1:1) to an aerobic exercise group or a waiting control group. The intervention group will receive a device-measured aerobic exercise prescription for eight weeks, consisting of moderate-intensity sessions lasting 30 to 50 min, three times per week, alongside their routine treatment. The control group will continue with routine treatment and will initiate the same exercise intervention after the 8-week follow-up period. No additional pharmacological treatment will be initiated or adjusted during the intervention period as part of the study protocol. For those not currently on medication, the intervention will consist of aerobic exercise only. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, mid-intervention (week 4), and post-intervention (week 8) to evaluate the efficacy of aerobic exercise. The primary outcome is the change in Hamilton Depression Rating Scale score from baseline. Secondary outcomes include cognitive function, depressive and anxiety symptoms, rumination, sleep quality, psychological resilience, safety, physical fitness, exercise capacity, and biological markers. All analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle. A mixed-effects model will be used for continuous outcomes, and modified Poisson regression will be applied for binary outcomes. Neuroimaging, laboratory and multi-omics tests will be conducted at both baseline and post-intervention, to explore the potential mechanisms through which aerobic exercise exerts its antidepressant effects. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of aerobic exercise in improving depression and cognition, elucidate its underlying mechanisms, and identify patient subgroups most likely to benefit. The findings may contribute to improved treatment outcomes for depression and inform the development of individualized clinical exercise prescriptions. ClincalTrials.gov NCT06594588, registered 5 Sep 2024.

papers.title: Development and validation of a machine learning model with a web-based calculator for predicting anxiety risk among nursing interns.
papers.abstract: The clinical internship, a period of profound transition for nursing students, is fraught with stressors that precipitate anxiety, yet current risk assessment tools often lack explainability, limiting their ability to support personalized and proactive psychological interventions. To develop and validate an explainable machine learning model (ML) that predicts anxiety risk in nursing interns and to create a web-based calculator for early detection to facilitate adaptive clinical interventions. A total of 1,233 nursing interns(Class of 2025) were enrolled between January and April 2025 for model development. Anxiety was defined using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale (GAD-7) as the standard assessment tool. Six ML methods, including logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), gradient boosting machine (GBM), neural networks (NN), random forest (RF), and XGBoost, were implemented to predict the risk of anxiety. External validation was conducted using data from 383 nursing interns(Class of 2026) recruited between July and August 2025 to evaluate the model's generalizability. The optimal model was selected on the basis of the AUC. This study also applied the SHAP approach to explain the model's outcomes. Additionally, the best-performing model was used to develop a web-based anxiety risk calculator. Sleep disorder, poor academic performance, high stress level, low social support, and a history of mental illness were identified as important predictors. The GBM model exhibited the best performance, achieving an AUC of 0.894 in internal validation and 0.895 in external validation. This study used explainable ML methods to predict anxiety among Chinese nursing interns and to identify five significant risk factors. The GBM model exhibited the best performance. Coupled with its explainability, this tool holds potential clinical utility for designing personalized, targeted psychological interventions for high-risk individuals. Not applicable.

papers.title: Lights and shadows of time-of-day administration of immune checkpoint inhibitors in solid tumors: a comprehensive review with exploratory analyses.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment landscape for several solid tumors. Among the mechanisms investigated to explain variability in ICIs efficacy, the potential effect of the time-of-day (ToD) at which ICIs are administered has emerged as an area of interest. This review summarizes the evidence on the impact of ToD administration of ICIs in solid tumors. A comprehensive manual search of two leading international databases, PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus/ELSEVIER, was conducted to identify relevant studies. An exploratory pooled analysis of the included studies was performed. The pooled effect size was expressed as HR with 95%CIs for either PFS or OS, according to random-effect meta-analysis. Our research led to the selection of 21 relevant retrospective and prospective studies evaluating the effect of ToD infusion of ICIs across several solid tumor types. The predominantly retrospective design of the studies and the absence of a standardized ToD threshold limit the reliability of the available data. In our pooled, exploratory analysis, earlier administration was associated with better PFS and OS. Although ICIs morning administration may be associated with favorable survival trend, the available evidence is too heterogeneous to support a widespread adoption of a chrono-modulated approach. Additional prospective, reproducible clinical trials using standardized administration windows and clearly defined treatment regimens are necessary to further explore this path.

papers.title: Associations of 24-h movement behaviours and health-related physical fitness with educational outcomes among adolescents: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: The transition period of adolescence involves many changes regarding biology, cognition, and psychology that could influence health behaviour and educational outcomes. This systematic review sought to examine the relationship between various components of 24-h movement behaviours (physical activity, sedentary behaviour, and sleep), health-related physical fitness, and educational outcomes in 9-19-year-old individuals. This review was registered on PROSPERO and performed following the PRISMA guidelines. Searching of PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library databases revealed peer-reviewed studies published in English during 2005-2025. This search strategy led to a selection of 2,090 articles; 1,546 of them were duplicates and discarded, 544 records underwent title and abstract screening, 71 full-text papers were reviewed for inclusion criteria, and 22 studies were included into the narrative synthesis. Mainly, the evidence was related to physical activity and health-related physical fitness, which showed generally positive relationships with educational and learning-related cognitive outcomes. However, the results differed depending on the study design, population features, measures used, and educational outcomes. Evidence for sleep and sedentary or screen-based behaviours is scarce, as well as for all three types of movement behaviours assessed simultaneously. As a result, there is evidence of positive relationships between physical activity and physical fitness and some educational outcomes; however, there is no sufficient evidence of positive relationships of adherence to all 24-h movement behaviours to educational outcomes.

papers.title: Psychometric properties of the Peruvian version of the Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ).
papers.abstract: Musculoskeletal problems are frequent in the adult population. The Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ) assesses the presence of musculoskeletal symptoms across nine body regions, and its total score represents an index of symptom burden across regions; however, psychometric evidence for its use in Peru is lacking. To translate the NMQ into Peruvian Spanish and evaluate its structural validity, internal consistency, measurement invariance, and validity based on relationships with external variables in a sample of Peruvian adults. A psychometric study was conducted with 1,215 participants. The mean age was 22.7 years (SD = 8.3), and 73.0% were women. The NMQ was translated and back-translated into Peruvian Spanish. Structural validity was evaluated through confirmatory factor analysis using the WLSMV estimator. Internal consistency was estimated using McDonald's omega and Cronbach's alpha. Measurement invariance according to sex and age was examined using multigroup CFA and MIMIC models, respectively. Validity based on relationships with external variables was evaluated through correlations with sleep problems, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms. The one-factor scoring model showed sufficient structural validity: χ²(27) = 210, CFI = 0.957, TLI = 0.942, SRMR = 0.067, and RMSEA = 0.075 (95% CI: 0.065-0.084). Standardized factor loadings ranged from 0.67 to 0.77. Internal consistency was sufficient (ω = 0.794; α = 0.799). The NMQ symptom-burden index showed moderate positive correlations with sleep problems (ρ = 0.465), anxiety symptoms (ρ = 0.458), and depressive symptoms (ρ = 0.402), all p < .001. Measurement invariance according to sex and age was supported. The Peruvian version of the NMQ showed psychometric evidence for its one-factor model, supporting its use for accurately assessing musculoskeletal symptoms in Peruvian adults.

papers.title: Symptom-level transcriptome-wide associations of NMN-nominated KEGG pathways in major depression: a distributed endocytosis-hypersomnia signal, gene-weighted immune and motor cassettes, and limits of pathway-level polarity.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder is clinically heterogeneous. Its diagnostic criteria combine affective, cognitive, sleep, appetite, weight, energy, and psychomotor symptoms that may have partly different genetic and biological correlates. Recent symptom-level genetic studies indicate that directional neurovegetative features, including hypersomnia versus insomnia and weight gain versus weight loss, should not automatically be treated as interchangeable manifestations of a single depression factor. Work on immunometabolic and reversed-neurovegetative depression has likewise linked hypersomnia and weight gain to biological correlates that differ from those associated with insomnia and weight loss. This study examined whether KEGG gene sets nominated from a mouse NMN-aging experiment show symptom-specific associations with genetically predicted human brain expression in major depression. Public S-PrediXcan gene-level Z scores were available for 12 depression symptoms across brain tissues. Gene-level tissue Z scores were combined across tissues, and pathway-level Stouffer statistics were reconstructed from the stored gene-by-symptom matrix. The analysis included enrichment statistics, permutation tests, bootstrap confidence intervals, gene-class decomposition, leave-one-gene-out analysis, tissue sign concordance, size-matched empirical null sampling, library ranking, pathway overlap, and symptom-profile clustering. Primary interpretation was restricted to associations supported by permutation or confidence-interval criteria and by robustness checks. Gene-class and clustering analyses were treated as secondary. Four lead associations remained most defensible. Endocytosis was negatively associated with hypersomnia, with a pipeline Stouffer Z of approximately - 5.52, permutation p = .0025, 194 contributing genes, agreement across six brain tissues, rank 1 of 240 library tests, and a size-matched union-null p = .005. The association was distributed and aligned with the core symptom direction rather than being driven by the polar-divergent shortlist. Antigen processing and presentation was positively associated with hypersomnia, but the result was small and TAPBP-weighted. Peroxisome was positively associated with psychomotor agitation and was supported by IDH2 and HSD17B4 rather than HMGCL. A vasopressin-labelled set was also positively associated with agitation, with leverage concentrated in dynein and CREB3-family genes rather than AVP. HMGCL showed an extreme gene-level weight-gain versus weight-loss contrast but did not drive the peroxisome-agitation result. The findings are library-specific and hypothesis-generating. They support symptom-level prioritization of genes and biological processes for replication and colocalization, not claims about measured RNA, pathway activity in patients, NMN responsiveness in human brain, treatment response, or biological patient subtypes.

papers.title: A state-dependent glymphatic dimension in major depressive disorder: implications for treatment resistance.
papers.abstract: The glymphatic system refers to cerebrospinal fluid-interstitial fluid exchange and proposed drainage pathways shaped by sleep, arousal, vascular dynamics, and astrocytic organization. This physiology offers a way to connect disturbances that often coexist in major depressive disorder (MDD): disrupted sleep, fatigue, cognitive slowing, and stress-related abnormalities. We propose that difficulty establishing or maintaining a coordinated sleep-astrocyte-vascular state may contribute to illness persistence in some patients. Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) provides a setting in which this possibility can be examined across the course of treatment. Preclinical studies link stress and depressive-like behavior to astrocytic injury, aquaporin-4 dysregulation, and altered fluid transport. Human imaging findings vary across depressive phenotypes. In a dedicated TRD study, a higher diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) ratio was partly driven by reduced denominator diffusivity, illustrating the importance of interpreting this indirect index at component level. Whole-brain spatiotemporal models provide a complementary account of the neural activity accompanying these physiological states. Ketamine/esketamine, transcranial magnetic stimulation, and chronobiological interventions offer different ways to investigate treatment-related change; serotonergic psychedelics provide an exploratory extension. Longitudinal studies can establish how changes in sleep, fluid-sensitive imaging, and neural dynamics relate temporally to clinical recovery. This Perspective therefore develops a potentially modifiable physiological dimension of persistent depressive illness and defines how it can be tested.

papers.title: Predicting Alzheimer progression using EEG-based digital twins.
papers.abstract: Early and accurate prognosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains limited by current biomarkers, which are often invasive, require expensive equipment, or fail to predict individual trajectories of cognitive decline. In this study, we evaluated the Digital Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis (DADD) model, a digital twin framework that extracts neurodegeneration-related digital biomarkers from non-invasive recordings such as electroencephalography (EEG), mapping early functional neural alterations to latent parameters linked to structural AD mechanisms. DADD was applied to a cohort of 459 participants with Subjective Cognitive Decline (SCD) or Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), evaluating its performance against established AD biomarkers like APOE genotype, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) markers in predicting prognostic outcomes over a 10-year follow-up. Digital biomarkers demonstrated strong prognostic value, predicting participants who converted at follow-up, significantly outperforming standard EEG metrics. They also robustly forecast both risk and timing of clinical conversion, matching the performance of established AD biomarkers and even outperforming them in SCD participants. Moreover, combining established AD biomarkers with digital biomarkers led to a significant increase in prognostic accuracy. DADD represents a robust clinical tool, enabling scalable, affordable, non-invasive AD detection and prognostic stratification across diverse clinical settings.

papers.title: Animal models in psychedelic research - Tripping over translation.
papers.abstract: Psychedelic substances show promise for treating psychiatric disorders including depression, anxiety, and PTSD, but the neurobiological mechanisms underlying their therapeutic effects remain poorly understood. Preclinical findings have so far been inconsistent, limiting mechanistic insights. We argue this translational gap is exacerbated by systematic disconnects between conditions thought to shape therapeutic outcomes in humans and those employed in animal research. In this review, we analyse 266 rodent psychedelic studies published between 2014 and 2026 in order to generate a systematic audit of experimental conditions and behavioural assays currently applied in the field. Specifically, we first assessed adherence to welfare practices paralleling "set and setting" factors critical to human therapy. We found that most studies contained stress-inducing factors: only a minority reported active-phase testing (14%), environmental enrichment (7%), or refined handling protocols (21%), while drug administration almost universally relied on stress-inducing, restraint-requiring methods. Second, we evaluated the capacity of behavioural assays to capture experiential dynamics, revealing that most studies rely on brief, constrained testing with isolated behavioural markers that fail to capture the multidimensional, temporally evolving nature of psychedelic states. Beyond these methodological gaps, we identify a third critical factor largely absent from preclinical research: individual differences and social context. Most animal studies use group-level, cross-sectional designs that cannot characterize heterogeneous treatment responses or social mechanisms implicated in therapeutic change. We propose that improving translation requires a fundamental reorientation: from brief testing of stressed, isolated animals toward longitudinal tracking of individuals in enriched social environments using comprehensive behavioural characterization. We end by offering practical advice on how to implement some of these considerations in animal psychedelic research.

papers.title: Mapping the two faces of the blood-brain barrier.
papers.abstract: In brain capillaries, flattened endothelial cells separate the blood from the brain across luminal and abluminal membranes that are approximately 200 nm apart. Amick and colleagues now resolve this hidden polarity in vivo, identify sequence motifs that direct proteins towards the brain-facing membrane, and show that membrane distribution can change with the time of day.

papers.title: Natural environments and sleep during pregnancy: Associations of green and blue spaces with prenatal sleep outcomes in a Canadian cohort.
papers.abstract: Sleep quality during pregnancy is critical for maternal and child health, yet environmental determinants of prenatal sleep remain understudied. Green and blue spaces have demonstrated positive effects on mental health, which is robustly associated with sleep, but direct impacts of green and blue spaces on sleep among pregnant individuals are unclear. This study examined associations between green and blue spaces and sleep duration, disturbance, and impairment during pregnancy. Data from the pan-Canadian Pregnancy during the Covid-19 Pandemic (PdP, n = 8583) were linked with green (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), tree canopy) and blue space (distance from the nearest water body) data from Canadian Urban Environmental Health Research Consortium (CANUE). Sleep outcomes included self-reported sleep duration, disturbance, and impairment. Multiple linear regression models adjusted for age, ethnicity, neighborhood deprivation, socioeconomic status, population density, COVID-19 restriction severity, season, physical activity, and trimester. Greater tree canopy cover and NDVI were significantly associated with longer sleep duration. Contrary to our hypothesis, greater distance from water bodies was also associated with longer sleep duration and lower sleep disturbance. After additional adjustments, only the associations with sleep duration remained significant. No associations were observed for sleep-related impairment. Green spaces, particularly tree canopy, may positively influence prenatal sleep duration, whereas the effects of blue spaces may depend more on the type of interaction with these environments and additional contextual factors. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating environmental factors, particularly tree-rich environment, into maternal health strategies and urban planning to support perinatal well-being.

papers.title: Effects of acupuncture on sleep and fatigue in older adults treated for chronic low back pain: Secondary analyses of the BackInAction randomized clinical trial.
papers.abstract: Acupuncture can reduce back pain and chronic pain symptoms, while potentially reducing the need for pharmacological interventions in older adults with chronic low back pain (cLBP). This exploratory analysis examined the effects of acupuncture for cLBP on sleep and fatigue outcomes in older adults. Using BackInAction trial data, we examined the effectiveness of standard acupuncture (SA: 8-15 sessions across 12 weeks) and enhanced acupuncture (EA: standard acupuncture plus 4-6 additional sessions) among 743 older adults with cLBP. We looked at sleep duration, sleep quality, and fatigue using the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) compared to usual medical care (UMC). Linear regression with Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) was used to model the outcomes measured at 3, 6, and 12 months post-baseline except for sleep quality which was only measured at 6 months post-baseline. Compared to UMC, participants in the EA arm reported lower fatigue at 12 months (Adjusted Mean Difference (AMD) [95% CI]:-2.28 [-3.59, 0.96]). There were no statistically significant differences in sleep quality or duration at any time point between any groups. Exploratory analyses revealed that among women, the EA arm reported lower fatigue at 12 months (AMD [95% CI]: -1.84 [-3.50, -0.18]). Women in EA reported better sleep quality (AMD [95% CI]: -2.08 [-3.89, -0.26]) and longer duration at 6 months relative to women in SA (AMD [95% CI]: 0.22 [0.02, 0.41]). Acupuncture may reduce fatigue in older patients with cLBP, whereas the effects of acupuncture for cLBP on sleep outcomes remain limited. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04982315 registered July 29, 2021.

papers.title: Caffeine consumption aboard the International Space Station and its relationship to sleep and cognitive performance.
papers.abstract: Caffeine is a widely consumed performance-enhancing stimulant on Earth that also affects sleep outcomes. Though historically available on spaceflight missions, caffeine use and its influence on sleep and human performance in microgravity have yet to be evaluated. We combined archival data on caffeine use, sleep, and cognitive performance aboard the International Space Station to determine astronauts' consumption patterns and to characterize the relationships between caffeine consumption, sleep, and cognitive performance during spaceflight. All crewmembers with available data consumed caffeine (mean of 105 mg per day), a value lower than daily use in the regular population, and there were small but significant effects of caffeine on that night's sleep as well as of sleep on caffeine consumed the following day. Caffeine consumption also led to faster reaction times on cognitively demanding tasks. Though the data are limited, they provide important information about crew consumption habits which will be of use in future mission planning.

papers.title: Gut-muscle axis: A new perspective on microgravity‑induced skeletal muscle atrophy.
papers.abstract: Long-duration spaceflight poses multisystemic challenges to human health, exposing astronauts to a complex environment of concurrent stressors, including ionizing radiation, altered circadian rhythms, and weightlessness. Among these, the rapid atrophy of skeletal muscle is a critical barrier to deep-space exploration. While spaceflight is multifactorial, evidence indicates that the mechanical unloading inherent to microgravity is the primary driver of acute muscle protein degradation. Conventional pathological models have primarily focused on the internal mechanisms of muscle fiber atrophy driven directly by this mechanical unloading. However, this perspective cannot fully explain the remarkable speed of muscle atrophy observed during space missions or the limited efficacy of high-intensity, in-orbit physical countermeasures. To address this critical knowledge gap, this review systematically proposes an integrative pathological model centered on the gut-muscle axis. We posit that the microgravity environment does not act solely on the muscle and may also independently induce gut microbiota dysbiosis and compromise gut barrier integrity, leading to metabolic endotoxemia. Critically, we propose a potential synergistic amplification mechanism: an increased load of gut-derived inflammatory signals (lipopolysaccharide, LPS) combines with the independent, mechanical unloading-induced upregulation of the LPS receptor (Toll-like receptor 4, TLR4) in muscle tissue, collectively triggering and amplifying a local inflammatory response. This local muscle inflammation subsequently progresses to systemic inflammation via a cytokine cascade. Ultimately, this process drives rapid muscle breakdown through dual pathological pathways: the activation of protein degradation pathways and the inhibition of protein synthesis via induced anabolic resistance. This novel framework provides a systemic explanation for muscle degradation during spaceflight and a theoretical foundation for developing new countermeasures targeting gut homeostasis, such as precision microbial interventions. Furthermore, the framework has significant translational medicine implications for preventing and treating terrestrial muscle-wasting diseases, including sarcopenia and cachexia.

papers.title: Literacy training in kindergarten children using pencil, virtual keyboard, or tablet stylus: Writing-medium effects on training-induced event-related potential modulations during letter viewing.
papers.abstract: The effects of handwriting training on letter recognition, compared with typing, have mainly been discussed in terms of either action-perception coupling or visual learning processes. To clarify the underlying mechanisms, this study examined how different writing media during literacy acquisition affect event-related potential (ERP) modulations during a sequential letter-matching task in kindergarten children. The analyzed sample comprised 77 children (4.9-6.9 years), who completed 28 sessions of standardized training involving 16 letters using handwriting with pencil and paper, handwriting with a stylus on a tablet, or typing on a virtual keyboard. Before and after training, children performed a sequential character-matching task with letters and pseudoletters while EEG was recorded. Training-related ERP effects to letters were observed in occipital P1, N1, and N2 components and centro-parietal ERPs within the P2 time window, but not in ERPs at central electrodes associated with motor representations. ERP changes emerged following both handwriting with pencil and paper and typing training but not following stylus-based handwriting. Only the pencil group showed training-related left-lateralized increases of N1 amplitude to real letters. The ERP effects of the intervention primarily reflect visual learning processes rather than the reactivation of graphomotor memory traces. The left-lateralized N1 increase following handwriting with pencil and paper indicates that the writing medium influences the visual processing of learned letters. The absence of effects following handwriting with stylus may reflect the higher motor-control demands of writing on a slippery tablet surface or the poorer quality of the visual letter output.

papers.title: Patient-Centred Sleep Outcome Definitions in Primary Biliary Cholangitis: A Call for Patient Engagement in Future Research.
International Expert Consensus Statement on Contemporary Prevention and Management of Postoperative Delirium in Cardiac Surgery.
papers.abstract: Postoperative delirium is among the most frequent neurocognitive complications of cardiac surgery, with reported incidence ranging from 14% to more than 50% depending on patient population and operative complexity. It is independently associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, extended intensive care unit and hospital stay, long-term cognitive decline, and increased mortality. Despite this burden, prevention and management strategies remain inconsistent across institutions worldwide. An international multidisciplinary expert panel applied a structured PICOT (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome, Timing) framework to predefined clinical questions spanning four perioperative phases: preoperative, intraoperative, postoperative and intensive care, and recovery after intensive care. Designated expert groups synthesized available evidence through structured literature reviews, and consensus recommendations were developed using a modified Delphi methodology. The panel developed 14 consensus statements. Preoperatively, routine screening with the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and Clinical Frailty Scale, and multicomponent optimization are recommended. Opioid-sparing multimodal analgesia is recommended, whereas perioperative dexmedetomidine in place of benzodiazepines, cerebral oximetry, processed electroencephalography-guided anesthesia depth monitoring, and optimized oxygen delivery may be considered. In intensive care, validated delirium screening paired with sedation assessment, daily awakening and breathing trials, structured multicomponent care bundles, correction of reversible precipitants, and circadian-supportive environments are central. After transfer from intensive care, continued ward screening and structured post-discharge cognitive follow-up are recommended. These statements provide a framework for preventing and managing postoperative delirium after cardiac surgery and advocate a coordinated multimodal approach. Standardizing screening, prevention bundles, and long-term follow-up within routine clinical pathways is recommended as a core institutional priority.

papers.title: Time-Restricted Eating and Caloric Restriction Impact Bone and the Gut Microbiota in Postmenopausal Women: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Caloric restriction (CR) can reduce bone mineral density (BMD). Time-restricted eating (TRE) modulates circadian rhythms and gut microbiota, but its effects on bone when combined with CR are unknown. This study examined the effects of TRE+CR on bone in postmenopausal females with overweight or obesity and whether it is associated with changes in the gut microbiota. Forty-nine postmenopausal females (body mass index ≥25 kg/m2, 50-79 years) were randomized to 24-weeks of CR (-500 kcal/d) or TRE (<9-h eating)+CR. BMD and bone quality were assessed at weeks 0 and 24. Fecal samples were collected at weeks 0, 12, and 24, and blood samples at weeks 0 and 24. Participants (61±5 years, 33±4 kg/m2) had an eating window of 12.3±0.9 hours/day, which was maintained in the CR group (n=21) [+0.3h/day (0.0,0.68)], and reduced in the TRE+CR group (n=26) [-4.0h/day (-4.4,-3.6)] (P<0.001), with 88% and 94% adherence, respectively. Hip BMD decreased similarly in both groups over time [-0.010g/cm2 (-0.018, -0.002)] (P=0.001), without between-group differences (P=0.98). TRE+CR attenuated radius BMD loss compared to CR [0.009g/cm2 (-0.002, 0.021) vs. [-0.020g/cm2 (-0.033, -0.007); (P=0.001)]. Gut microbiota (beta-diversity) shifted within TRE+CR from baseline to week 24 (P<0.05), with increasing dissimilarity from the CR group emerging by week 12 (P<0.0001). Changes in microbial guild ratios were positively correlated with changes in radius BMD (P<0.05). Subgroup analysis indicated baseline microbial guilds predicted radius BMD preservation (AUC=0.73; 0.54, 0.92). Weight decreased [-6.8kg (-8.3, -5.4)] similarly between the groups (P=0.29), but visceral adiposity decreased more with TRE+CR (P=0.01). Serum bone turnover markers were unchanged, while glycemic indices improved (P<0.05) without between-group differences. TRE mitigated weight-loss-induced bone loss at a clinically relevant non-weight-bearing site, but not at the hip, and these effects may be associated with changes in the gut microbiota. Larger studies are needed to establish mechanisms and sustained health effects.
papers.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition

papers.title: Striatal Hand and Foot Deformities Heralding Parkinson Disease: A Seronegative Arthritis Mimic.
Longitudinal Changes in Symptom Burden and Health-Related Quality of Life after Hospitalization for COVID-19.
papers.abstract: Persistent symptoms after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) are common after hospitalization, but longitudinal changes in symptom burden and their relationship with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) remain incompletely understood. In this prospective single-center observational study, hospitalized adults with PCR-confirmed COVID-19 were assessed during the acute phase and at 3-month follow-up. Symptom burden was operationally defined as the count of 16 predefined binary symptoms. Changes were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank and McNemar tests with false discovery rate correction. Associations between within-patient changes in symptom burden and changes in SF-36 domains were assessed using Spearman correlations with false discovery rate correction. Among 49 patients with complete symptom data, median symptom burden decreased from 4 (IQR 5) at baseline to 2 (IQR 3) at follow-up (Z = -3.863, p < 0.001). Symptom burden decreased in 35 patients (71.4%) and increased in 8 (16.3%). Loss of appetite, diarrhea/vomiting, dizziness, sleep disturbances, headache, and fever decreased significantly, whereas hair loss increased at follow-up. Among 48 patients with complete paired data, changes in symptom burden correlated inversely with changes in seven SF-36 domains, most strongly for vitality (ρ = -0.343), social functioning (ρ = -0.318), and emotional well-being (ρ = -0.289), but none remained significant after FDR correction. Symptom burden decreased within three months after COVID-19 hospitalization. Although higher symptom burden was associated with poorer HRQoL at follow-up, associations between changes in symptom burden and changes in HRQoL were not statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons.

papers.title: Improved sleep and clinical outcomes following a single-session intervention among adolescents with borderline personality disorder features.
papers.abstract: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is a serious mental illness that often emerges in adolescence. Although efficacious treatments have been developed, they are often lengthy, expensive, inaccessible, and require specialized training to deliver. Optimizing BPD prevention and early treatment is an important public health priority. Disrupted sleep is closely linked to key BPD features, and prior research has documented a range of sleep problems among BPD samples that appear to worsen symptom course and duration. This intervention trial (NCT04507308) assessed the effects of a single-session sleep-focused treatment on adolescent sleep and BPD-related symptoms. Fifty-seven adolescents (ages 13-18) with 3+ clinically impairing BPD features and at least some self-reported sleep-related difficulties participated with a caregiver. Participants completed baseline surveys, interviews, and 10-day ecological momentary assessment (EMA) protocol to examine BPD symptoms and sleep in daily life. Youth also collected at-home ambulatory electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings before undergoing the treatment informed by the Transdiagnostic Sleep and Circadian Intervention. Post-treatment, youth practiced their new sleep routine for approximately one month before undergoing reassessment (EMA, EEG, surveys). Many indices of sleep quantity and quality improved across both objective (EEG) and subjective assessments (EMA and self- and caregiver-report). Youth reported an earlier clock time at sleep onset and earlier waketime, more sleep, and fewer awakenings in daily life. Every sleep-related questionnaire score improved at post-intervention and was maintained at one-month follow-up. Multiple (though not all) indices of BPD symptoms also improved significantly. Findings suggest sleep may be a promising intervention target for at-risk youth.

papers.title: Epilepsy Surgery in Patients with Non-Lesional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Evaluated with Stereoelectroencephalography: Retrospective Analysis in a High-Complexity Center and Literature Review.
papers.abstract: Background and objective When epilepsy is associated with non-lesional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and there is no anatomical-electro-clinical correlation of seizures, invasive studies, such as stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG), are necessary to determine the epileptogenic zone (EZ) and, subsequently, the type of surgery to be performed. The aim of this work is to report the results of epilepsy surgery in patients with non-lesional MRI evaluated with SEEG and to conduct a literature review. Materials and methods Retrospective descriptive observational study. Non-invasive pre-surgical studies included neuropsychological and psychiatric evaluation, MRI with epilepsy protocol, positron emission tomography, and video-electroencephalography. Invasive studies included SEEG. Surgery was performed with curative intent in all patients. The Engel criteria were used to evaluate post-surgical results. Pathological anatomy and its correlation with surgical outcomes were considered. Results Eleven patients met the inclusion criteria for our analysis. All presented with inconsistent non-invasive preoperative examinations that did not allow for localization of the epileptic zone (EZ). SEEG was performed, successfully theorizing the ZE according to the electroclinical hypothesis in all patients. Four patients underwent anterior temporal lobectomy and seven underwent extratemporal corticectomy. We obtained a 63.6% rate of good postoperative results. Conclusion The SEEG allowed theorizing the ZE in all patients. The overall postoperative results were consistent with the literature. However, in the subgroup analysis, unlike previous studies, in our case series, extratemporal non-lesional epilepsy showed better postoperative results than temporal non-lesional epilepsy.

papers.title: Mismatch Negativity and General Cognitive Ability - A Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Intelligence or general cognitive ability (GCA) is fundamental to human behavior and cognition. It impacts important life outcomes like educational success, and even health and longevity have been related to differences in GCA. Understanding the biological basis of such individual variations presents a crucial goal of neuroscience. The mismatch negativity (MMN) is an event-related brain potential that can be measured when-within a series of frequent standard stimuli, rare deviants are presented-and is suggested to reflect conscious (active) or unconscious (passive) detection processes of the brain. Importantly, variations in MMN amplitude and latency have been linked to differences in GCA. Yet findings vary considerably. This preregistered meta-analysis provides a comprehensive and structured overview of the current state of research. Following the study selection process in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, and the rating of study design quality with the Study Design and Implementation Assessment Device for Individual Difference Research (DIAD-ID), the association between GCA and MMN amplitude and latency was examined in 645 healthy adults across 12 included studies. The estimated across-sample associations between MMN and GCA were small, but significant (MMN amplitude-GCA: r = -0.09, MMN latency-GCA: r = -0.16; p < 0.01) and moderators were identified. Between-sample heterogeneity was moderate, with no evidence of publication bias. Our findings suggest that higher cognitive ability is associated with slightly stronger and faster MMN responses. However, the low estimated across-sample effect sizes and the small number of included studies also highlight the need for more research.

papers.title: Prediction of surgical outcome using cyclic spectral coherent networks of intracranial EEG signals.
papers.abstract: Epilepsy is a network disorder characterized by abnormal brain connectivity. Identifying network-level biomarkers is critical for improving surgical outcome prediction and understanding seizure dynamics. This study proposes a novel framework to assess the brain network organization of epileptic patients using cyclostationary-based connectivity matrices derived from intracranial EEG (iEEG) signals. The iEEG recordings of epileptic patients with surgical outcomes classified as Engel I (n=19) and Engel II+ (n=19) groups are considered for this study. Cyclic Spectral Coherence (CSC) based connectivity matrices are estimated from the preictal, ictal and postictal seizure phases using Welch's method. Further, network hubs are identified using centrality measures and the Resection Hub Alignment Degree (RHAD) metric is computed to quantify the alignment between the hubs and surgically resected nodes. The results of the cyclostationary spectrum reveal non-zero spectral correlation density, confirming the presence of rhythmic patterns in iEEG signals with dominant peaks observed in the SOZ regions. Furthermore, preictal RHAD-EVC differentiates the seizure-free and non-seizure-free patient groups (p < 0.01) and achieves an AUC of 0.64 for postoperative surgical outcome prediction. The results of the proposed method are in good agreement with those reported in previous studies. Overall, the cyclic spectral coherent network-based RHAD metric may serve as a robust index that captures the network disruptions beyond geometric overlap. The proposed framework demonstrates potential to serve as an ancillary tool for characterizing network alterations rather than as a standalone predictive indicator.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of anti-IL-4Rα stapokibart for adults with moderate-to-severe prurigo nodularis: results from a phase 3 randomized trial.
papers.abstract: Prurigo nodularis (PN) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease with limited treatment options. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of anti-IL-4Rα stapokibart in adults with moderate-to-severe PN. This was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study (NCT06424470) conducted in 39 centers in China between June 24, 2024, and April 14, 2025. Eligible patients who had a diagnosis of PN for ≥3 months were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive subcutaneous stapokibart 300 mg (a loading dose, 600 mg) or placebo every 2 weeks for 24 weeks. Totally 200 patients were enrolled (n=100 per group). At week 24, significantly greater proportions of stapokibart-treated patients versus placebo achieved ≥4-point improvement in Worst Itch Numeric Rating Scale (64.0% vs. 33.0%; primary endpoint) and Investigator's Global Assessment for chronic nodular prurigo stage score of 0/1 (45.0% vs. 14.0%; key secondary endpoint) (both P<0.0001). Benefits were also observed in patients' quality of life, skin pain, sleep disturbance, and anxiety/depression. The incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events was similar between the stapokibart and placebo groups (79.0% vs. 73.0%). Chinese patients only. 24 weeks of treatment with stapokibart demonstrated high efficacy and favorable safety in adults with moderate-to-severe PN.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology

papers.title: Beyond weakness: The overlooked cognitive face of myasthenia gravis.
papers.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune disease mediated by autoantibodies. Traditionally, it was strictly defined as a neuromuscular junction-specific disorder, believed not to affect the central nervous system (CNS). However, recent clinical observations and neuropsychological studies have demonstrated that a significant proportion of MG patients exhibit cognitive dysfunction, with clinical manifestations encompassing impairments in multiple cognitive domains such as verbal fluency, information processing speed, and memory. Neuroimaging further reveals structural and functional alterations in MG patients, including gray matter volume atrophy and abnormalities in default mode network connectivity. These findings challenge previous cognitive frameworks, suggesting that the disease may exert broader effects on the CNS. Current understanding indicates that the pathogenesis of MG-associated cognitive impairment involves complex central-peripheral interactions: mechanisms such as blood-brain barrier disruption, cross-reaction of specific autoantibodies, and neuroinflammatory responses can lead to direct CNS involvement, whereas chronic hypoxia (secondary to respiratory muscle weakness or sleep apnea), prolonged drug effects, and psychological factors like depression and anxiety associated with the disease may also indirectly impair cognitive function. Nevertheless, the field still faces numerous challenges, including the lack of large-scale longitudinal studies to elucidate the natural course and trajectory of cognitive impairment, as well as the identification of biomarkers. This narrative review collates recent research advances regarding MG-related cognitive impairment and discusses its clinical manifestations, confounding influencing factors, underlying pathophysiological mechanisms, and existing diagnostic difficulties.

papers.title: Early Childhood CASPR2 Autoimmunity with Prominent Autonomic Dysfunction: Diagnostic Challenges and Effective Immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: CASPR2-associated neurological diseases cover a broad clinical spectrum, with limbic encephalitis and Morvan syndrome representing the most characteristic autoimmune phenotypes. We report the case of a 2-year-old boy who presented with abdominal and generalized pain, refusal to eat or drink, weight loss, loss of mobility, and behavioral changes, including sleep disturbances. Further clinical evaluation revealed pharmacoresistant arterial hypertension and hyperhidrosis. Extensive diagnostic testing excluded infectious and toxic causes. CASPR2 antibodies were detected in both serum and cerebrospinal fluid. Initial therapy with corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulins resulted in only minimal clinical improvement. Significant clinical recovery was only achieved after escalation of immunotherapy with plasmapheresis and subsequent B-cell-depleting therapy with rituximab. At the most recent follow-up visit, seven months after the first rituximab infusion, the patient showed complete recovery without residual symptoms. This case underscores the diagnostic challenges of CASPR2-associated autoimmunity in early childhood and highlights the importance of early recognition of this rare but treatable disease.

papers.title: Healthcare Team Awareness, Knowledge, and Perceptions of Neonatal Delirium: A Cross-Sectional Survey Study.
papers.abstract: Neonatal delirium is increasingly recognized as an important neuropsychiatric condition in critically ill infants, yet awareness and understanding among healthcare providers remain limited. Underdiagnosis may contribute to prolonged hospitalization, increased morbidity, and adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. This study assessed healthcare team members' awareness, perceptions, and knowledge of neonatal delirium across a large children's hospital and affiliated neonatal care locations. A cross‑sectional electronic survey was distributed to multidisciplinary NICU team members within a quaternary academic children's health system and affiliated sites. The survey included demographic items, multiple‑choice questions, Likert‑scale statements, and open‑ended responses. Descriptive statistics summarized quantitative data, and content categorization was applied to open‑ended responses. A total of 117 respondents completed the survey, representing nursing, advanced practice providers, physicians, respiratory therapists, rehabilitation therapists, and pharmacy. Nearly half of respondents had never heard the term neonatal delirium. Among those familiar with the condition, definitions most commonly referenced agitation, altered consciousness, and sleep-wake disturbance. Ninety percent of respondents agreed that newborn infants can experience delirium, while only 60% indicated that delirium can also occur in preterm infants. Sixty percent indicated that delirium is assessable in infants, and 73% reported previously caring for an infant with suspected delirium. Respondents identified multiple barriers to screening and management, including limited awareness, lack of content expertise, and concerns about medication safety. Awareness and understanding of neonatal delirium vary considerably among NICU providers, with notable educational and structural barriers to consistent recognition and management. These findings support the need for foundational education, multidisciplinary training, and continued research to inform development of effective strategies for assessing and managing neonatal delirium in neonatal care settings.

papers.title: Behavioral Latency as Weak Event-Time Supervision for EEG Reaction-Time Decoding.
papers.abstract: Single-trial EEG analyses are often organized around events and latencies, such as stimulus onset, response execution, ERP component timing, and movement onset. Yet EEG-based reaction-time prediction is commonly posed as scalar regression on a fixed stimulus-locked window, so reaction time is treated as a window-level label rather than timing evidence about response-relevant dynamics. Here we reformulate trial-wise reaction-time decoding as event-time posterior modeling. Instead of predicting a single reaction time (RT) directly, the model estimates a posterior distribution over response-relevant event times, p(t event |X), and uses the posterior mean as the RT estimate. This treats behavioral latency as a weak observation of latent response-relevant timing, making the output representation itself part of the computational hypothesis. We evaluate this formulation on the healthy brain network contrast change detection EEG task under a subject-disjoint, release-separated protocol. Across five seeds, distributional event-time supervision consistently improves held-out RT prediction relative to scalar regression and temporal-readout controls. Controlled objective comparisons isolate supervision of the event-time distribution, rather than expectation-based readout alone, as the source of this gain; architecture controls establish that the effect persists across four temporal backbones and is not explained by model scale. Beyond point prediction, the event-time posterior serves as a diagnostic for separating temporal evidence from scalar shortcuts. Posterior geometry characterizes temporal concentration, target alignment, and interval behavior, while observation-noise calibration separates latent event-time concentration from predictive uncertainty over observed RT. We also use shifted-crop inference to probe shortcut use versus temporal localization. A matched shift-jitter intervention improves shifted-crop robustness, increases mean sensitivity, and moves predictions more often in the expected crop-relative direction. Sensitivity remains below ideal crop-relative localization, leaving a clear equivariance gap. Together, these results establish event-time posterior modeling as a probabilistic and interpretable formulation for linking single-trial EEG dynamics to behavioral timing.

papers.title: Clock misalignment, not structural loss, underlies memory impairment following disruption of the mushroom body.
papers.abstract: The Drosophila mushroom body (MB) is a central circuit for many forms of associative learning, including olfactory conditioning, courtship conditioning, and aversive phototaxic suppression (APS). Kenyon cells (KCs), the intrinsic neurons of the MB, can be severely disrupted but not entirely eliminated by hydroxy urea (HU) treatment during development. Here, we show that HU-treated flies are profoundly impaired in short- and long-term memory under baseline conditions and that enhanced sleep restores learning in these animals. We establish the robustness of this finding using multiple behavioral assays and two independent methods to enhance sleep. Mechanistic analyses reveal that HU treatment disrupts circadian clock output, mistiming activity in γ-lobe-projecting dopaminergic neurons (DANs) and MB output neurons (MBONs). We further show that this mistiming is mediated, in part, by pigment-dispersing factor (PDF) signaling onto γ2-projecting DANs. Enhanced sleep restores the proper temporal coordination of these circuits. Strikingly, selectively reducing PDF receptor (Pdfr) signaling in these DANs also restored memory in HU-treated flies despite markedly reduced sleep, demonstrating that correcting mistimed clock signals can reproduce the restorative effects of sleep. These findings indicate that memory impairments after HU treatment can arise from disrupted temporal coordination within the MB circuit and demonstrate that downstream MBON-DAN interactions can support learning when properly regulated.

papers.title: A natural mutation of timeless enhances mosquito thermal adaptation and malaria parasite transmission.
papers.abstract: Anopheles stephensi, a malaria-transmitting mosquito, has invaded Africa and rapidly adapts to the high temperatures in urban settings. However, the molecular basis of its thermal adaptation remains unclear. Here, we identified a variant of a 5-kb deletion in the circadian clock gene timeless (tim-5kb) that rose to high frequency after 3 years of rearing at high laboratory temperatures. The tim+/-5kb heterozygous males maintain stable expression of the period gene at high temperatures, conferring a competitive mating advantage through the increased expression of the adipokinetic hormone gene AKH1 to promote energy mobilization and flight activity, together with the upregulation of fatty acyl-CoA reductase genes FAR3 and FAR5 to enhance the production of heptacosane pheromone. Moreover, heterozygous females exhibit increased susceptibility to Plasmodium infection, increasing malaria transmission potential. These findings reveal a circadian-based genetic mechanism that may underlie thermal adaptation in An. stephensi and hold important implications for malaria control in Africa.

papers.title: Supraorbital Near-Infrared Stimulation and Portable EEG: An Exploratory Fixed-Order Study of Spectral Markers and Signal Quality.
papers.abstract: Near-infrared stimulation of the supraorbital region is an approach for investigating brain physiology, but its effects require validation. This exploratory fixed-order study evaluated EEG markers during bilateral 940-nm supraorbital stimulation in 25 healthy women. Participants received active stimulation at Visit 1 and sham at Visit 2, at least 14 days apart. EEG was recorded using MUSE 2. The principal analysis compared PRE-to-DURING changes in global gamma log-power between visits. The mean difference-in-change was 0.101 a.u. (unadjusted BCa bootstrap 95% CI: 0.027-0.213; Cohen's dz = 0.43; paired t-test p = 0.040). However, Wilcoxon inference was not significant (p = 0.090), difference scores deviated from normality (Shapiro-Wilk p = 0.008), and leave-one-out estimates were sensitive to participants. Signal quality also differed between visits. Visit order confounding and unverified signal origin preclude conclusions about stimulation effects or cortical gamma modulation. This study provides feasibility data and priorities for randomized, counterbalanced follow-up.

papers.title: Digital Health Coaching in Adult Cancer Survivorship Care: A Scoping Review and Nursing-Oriented Evidence Map.
papers.abstract: To (1) map digital delivery modalities and behavior-change ingredients used in adult cancer survivorship; (2) describe the distribution of evidence across cancer populations, intervention domains, and outcomes; and (3) identify nursing implementation functions and evidence gaps. A scoping review was conducted using JBI methodology, informed by Arksey and O'Malley and Levac et al, and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, APA PsycINFO, and CINAHL were searched from database inception through April 1, 2026, without language or study-design filters. Three reviewers independently screened records, assessed full texts, charted data, classified evidence, and grouped companion publications into intervention/study families; discrepancies were resolved through discussion and consensus. Critical appraisal was not undertaken because the purpose was to map the extent, characteristics, and gaps of the evidence rather than estimate intervention effectiveness. The search identified 1,197 records. We included 118 publications representing 90 intervention/study families; 104 publications representing 78 families formed the core evidence map, and 14 publications representing 12 families were summarized as peripheral evidence. Mobile apps and web platforms were the most common delivery channels, but active intervention content varied and included goal setting, self-monitoring, tailored feedback, action planning, problem solving, reminders, and human support. Nursing implementation functions additionally included symptom review, monitoring, triage, referral, and escalation. Evidence was concentrated in physical activity, lifestyle, fatigue, symptom self-management, patient-reported outcomes, and rehabilitation. Sleep-specific and metabolic-health-focused interventions were sparse, and few programs addressed sleep, physical activity, and weight/metabolic risk together. Reporting of intervention content, dose, fidelity, clinical responsibility, long-term maintenance, equity, and workflow integration was inconsistent. Digital health coaching is best understood as a set of blended digital-human support arrangements rather than as a technology category or a single survivorship care model. Its clinical value depends on the behavior-change ingredients, support intensity, nursing responsibilities, escalation pathways, and workflows connected to the technology. Oncology nurses can use the evidence map to match survivor needs with support intensity, define monitoring and escalation responsibilities, and design equitable digital-human survivorship workflows.

papers.title: Alpha coherence is a network signature of cognitive recovery from disorders of consciousness.
papers.abstract: Alpha (8-12 Hz) frequency band oscillations are among the most informative features in electroencephalographic (EEG) assessment of patients with disorders of consciousness (DoC). Because interareal alpha synchrony is thought to facilitate long-range communication in healthy brains, coherence measures of resting-state alpha oscillations may provide insights into a patient's capacity for higher-order cognition beyond channel-wise estimates of alpha power. In multi-channel EEG, global coherence methods may be used to augment standard spectral analysis methods by assessing both the strength and spatiotemporal structure of coherent oscillatory networks. We performed global coherence analysis in 95 separate clinical EEG recordings (28 healthy controls and 33 patients with acute or chronic DoC, 25 of whom returned for follow-up) collected between two academic medical centers. We found that posterior alpha coherence is associated with recovery of cognitive status represented by a CRS-R total score of 22 or above. We developed a measure of network organization based on the principal eigenvector of the cross-spectral matrix in the alpha band. This network measure performs well in classifying recovery from DoC (AUC = .78) compared to measures of functional connectivity based on the weighted phase lag index (AUC = .45 - .53). Our findings suggest that normalization of network activity in the alpha band may represent a sensitive signature of cognitive recovery in patients with DoC and that network-based methods may augment the utility of EEG assessments for DoC.
papers.journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior

papers.title: Health behaviors as a pathway between early life adversity and cardiometabolic risk for previously institutionalized youth.
papers.abstract: Early life adversity including caregiving stress and neglect has been linked to elevated cardiometabolic risk. Children adopted from institutional care represent a well-characterized model of this exposure limited to the first few years of life, with elevated cardiometabolic risk documented as early as adolescence, even in the absence of overweight or obesity.
