The present study examines whether health behaviors such as diet, sleep quality measured as daytime drowsiness, and physical activity serve as pathways through which early life adversity shapes cardiometabolic risk during adolescence. Ninety-five previously institutionalized youth (MeanAdoptionAge = 16.2, SD = 12 months, 63% female) and 95 birth-reared youth (MeanAge = 15.8, SD = 2.4 years, 52% female) reported on diet, daytime drowsiness, and physical activity. Two years later, they visited the lab for cardiometabolic health assessment via SphygmoCor, Dual X-ray absorptiometry scan, and blood draws. Cardiometabolic risk was indexed by insulin resistance, cholesterol, arterial stiffness (aortic augmentation index and pulse wave velocity), and android fat percentage. Eating an inflammatory diet and greater drowsiness, but not physical activity, emerged as significant indirect pathways linking early adversity and cardiometabolic risk. Specifically, previously institutionalized youth ate more inflammatory diets and were drowsier during the day than birth-reared youth, which in turn, was associated with higher cardiometabolic risk. These findings raise questions about the mechanisms linking early life adversity to later eating and sleep behaviors and suggest that these behaviors may be modifiable targets for reducing cardiometabolic risk in adolescents with histories of early adversity.

papers.title: Increased temporal persistence of reference-invariant bilateral EEG states in adult ADHD.
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is associated with heterogeneous EEG abnormalities, but the short-timescale persistence of bilateral relational states remains unclear. Resting EEG from 56 adults with ADHD and 179 healthy adults was studied across 10 homologous pairs and four frequency bands. Eyes-closed (EC) recordings were used exclusively for target discovery, and the EC-frozen targets were evaluated in eyes-open (EO) recordings from largely the same participants. Effects were then examined under common-average re-referencing and using homologous voltage differences formed before nonlinear envelope extraction. Initial sensor-envelope analysis identified 44 EC effects, 35 of which generalized to EO under the released reference, but none survived common-average re-referencing. In the distinct, algebraically reference-invariant bipolar-envelope representation, four of 24 frozen difference targets were significant in the same direction in both EC and EO: Fp1-Fp2 theta and beta, C3-C4 delta, and P3-P4 delta. All four remained significant in age-overlap analyses, including nonlinear age adjustment. Adult ADHD is associated with increased short-lag retention of a restricted set of common-reference-invariant bilateral voltage-difference envelope states. The broad sensor-envelope findings were representation dependent, not necessarily artefactual. EC-to-EO generalization and within-sample reference-invariance testing do not constitute independent-cohort replication.

papers.title: Characterizing source-level electroencephalography activities to single-pulse TMS-EEG.
papers.abstract: To distinguish active from sham single-pulse TMS responses over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) using source-level EEG, emphasizing target-region effects and exploratory whole-brain patterns. Thirty-three healthy adults underwent active and sham TMS-EEG. We assessed local TMS-evoked potentials (TEPs), electric-field simulations, and source-derived significant current density (SCD) and scattering (SCS). Target-region ROI analyses examined early (30-60 ms) and late (250-350 ms) responses; whole-brain differences were tested using cluster-based permutation tests. Peripheral EEG measures were evaluated before and after independent component analysis (ICA) and used as covariates. Active stimulation produced larger early local TEPs than sham (2.15 ± 1.39 vs. 0.85 ± 0.66 μV; Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.001), a more negative N100, and a larger P200. Target-region SCS and SCD were greater with active stimulation in both windows (all adjusted p < 0.01). Whole-brain tests identified significant late SCS (275-333 ms) and SCD (269-374 and 271-366 ms) clusters, but no early clusters. Measured peripheral differences were nonsignificant after ICA. Covariate adjustment preserved the SCS and one SCD cluster, whereas the other SCD cluster was not significant after muscle-related adjustment. Target-region source measures differentiated active from sham stimulation at early and late latencies, whereas significant whole-brain clusters were observed only at late latencies. Early source-level findings complement sensor-level TEPs, but late-stage source evidence requires cautious interpretation.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology

papers.title: Psychological, lifestyle, and self-management profiles among Indonesian adults with diabetes in the fifth wave of the Indonesia family life survey.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus requires continued psychological adjustment, healthy lifestyle behaviors, and ongoing disease management. This study examined heterogeneity in psychological functioning, well-being, lifestyle behaviors, and diabetes care indicators among adults with diabetes in the fifth wave of the Indonesia Family Life Survey (IFLS-5). The analysis included 685 respondents with a self-reported diagnosis of diabetes by a health professional and 14 binary indicators in six domains: psychological distress (depressive symptoms, sleep disturbance, neuroticism), subjective well-being (life satisfaction, general happiness), lifestyle behaviors (smoking behavior, physical activity, sweet food consumption), diabetes self-management (medication use, health monitoring), comorbidity and functional burden (comorbid chronic conditions, functional limitation), and healthcare service utilization (outpatient health service utilization, inpatient hospitalization history). A three-class solution was retained because BIC and CAIC were lowest at three classes, the Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin test did not support a fourth class, the smallest class comprised 16.2% of the sample, and the classes were interpretable; class separation was moderate (entropy = 0.719). The classes were Low-Distress Low-Engagement (61.1%), with low distress, high well-being, and comparatively low medication use and monitoring; High-Engagement High-Comorbidity (22.7%), with a high probability of current medication use and health monitoring and the heaviest comorbidity and functional burden; and High-Distress Low-Engagement (16.2%), with elevated depressive symptoms, lower well-being, and the lowest probabilities of medication use and monitoring. The three-class structure was reproduced when seven indicators kept their original scales, although membership in the distress class was less stable. The same three classes were obtained without the Neuroticism indicator, whose internal consistency was low, and adjusting the standard errors for household and enumeration-area clustering changed them only slightly. These co-occurring patterns require longitudinal and external validation.

papers.title: Distinct predictors of sleep timing and sleep problems in infants and young toddlers: The role of parental chronotype, sleep quality, and psychological distress.
papers.abstract: Child sleep timing and perceived sleep problems may have different family-level correlates. We examined associations of maternal and paternal chronotype, sleep quality, psychological distress, maternal sleep-related cognitions, and paternal involvement in infant care with infant and young toddler sleep timing and perceived sleep-problem severity. This single-center cross-sectional study included 107 mother-father-child triads aged 6-18 months. Child sleep was evaluated using the Brief Infant Sleep Questionnaire-Revised. Sleep midpoint was calculated as a measure of child sleep timing, and perceived sleep-problem severity was assessed on a 1-5 ordinal scale. Both parents completed measures of chronotype, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), anxiety, and depressive symptoms; maternal sleep-related cognitions and paternal involvement were also assessed. Multiple linear and ordinal logistic regression models evaluated associations with the two outcomes. Greater maternal morningness was independently associated with an earlier child sleep midpoint, including after adjustment for child age (B = -0.051, 95% CI -0.075 to -0.026; p < 0.001). In the combined ordinal model, poorer maternal sleep quality was the only factor independently associated with greater perceived sleep-problem severity (aOR = 1.28 per PSQI point, 95% CI 1.12-1.46; p < 0.001). No paternal variable was independently associated with either outcome in the adjusted models. Child sleep midpoint was not associated with sleep-problem severity (Spearman's ρ = -0.088, p = 0.369). Maternal chronotype was associated with infant and young child sleep timing, whereas maternal sleep quality was associated with perceived child sleep-problem severity. These findings suggest that child sleep timing and sleep problems may represent distinct dimensions of sleep in infants and young toddlers.

papers.title: Through tired eyes: Self-reported sleepiness and sleep patterns of children with and without ADHD.
papers.abstract: Excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) is common among children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) but is frequently under-recognised, with most paediatric sleep research relying on parent-report or objective measures that cannot capture the child's subjective experience of sleepiness. This study examined self-reported EDS and sleep patterns in Australian primary school-aged children with and without ADHD and examined whether the inattentive (ADHD-I) and combined (ADHD-C) presentations show distinct sleep profiles. Two hundred and seventy-three children aged 7-12 years (typically developing [TD], n = 131; ADHD-I, n = 57; ADHD-C, n = 85) completed the Children's Report of Sleep Patterns-Sleepiness Scale and a modified Children's Report of Sleep Patterns self-reported deriving measures of daytime sleepiness and sleep habits, with group differences examined. Children with ADHD-C took significantly longer to fall asleep and were more likely to use nighttime medication than TD children and woke more frequently overnight than children with ADHD-I. Children with ADHD-C also reported increased amount of sleepiness than TD children, an effect that approached significance. Children with ADHD-I reported significantly higher sleepiness at school than TD children and rated themselves less positively as sleepers than TD children, despite no significant differences in other self-reported sleep variables. Children with ADHD-C and ADHD-I did not differ significantly in overall sleepiness, but differences emerged in specific domains, including longer sleep onset latency and increased nighttime medication use in ADHD-C as well as increased sleepiness at school for children with ADHD-I. A trend also emerged toward poorer self-rated sleeper status in children with ADHD-I without corresponding differences in other self-reported sleep variables. These findings support routine sleep screening in ADHD and the clinical value of asking children directly about their own sleep experience.

papers.title: Longitudinal associations between infant parenting and toddler sleep: Examining the moderating role of infant regulation.
papers.abstract: Early-life sleep has lasting health effects, with caregivers playing a central role in its development. Parenting is associated with sleep duration and quality during both infancy and toddlerhood. Less is known about longitudinal associations from infancy into toddlerhood. The current analysis evaluated parenting routine, nurturance, and anxiety at age seven months as predictors of child sleep duration and sleep problems at ages 18-24 months, along with moderation by infant regulation at seven months. Participants were 66 first-time parents (Mage = 30.8 years, 60.9% White, 97% mothers). Tests of associations between infant parenting and toddler sleep were non-significant. However, the interaction between infant parenting routine and infant regulation in the prediction of toddler sleep duration was significant (p = .00405). At low levels of infant regulation, lower levels of routine predicted shorter sleep, while higher levels of routine predicted longer sleep. The opposite relation was observed at high levels of infant regulation. At low levels of infant regulation, parents who reported using more routines in infancy had toddlers with longer sleep duration. At high levels of infant regulation, parents who reported using more routines in infancy had toddlers with shorter sleep duration. This finding is novel but will need to be replicated in larger, more diverse samples. Further exploration of infant temperament and parent-infant interactive effects are warranted to better understand implications for early life sleep.

papers.title: Impact of positional obstructive sleep apnea phenotype on mandibular advancement therapy outcomes: A multicenter cohort study.
papers.abstract: Mandibular advancement devices (MADs) are an established treatment for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but reliable predictors of response remain limited. Positional OSA (POSA) has been proposed as a favorable phenotype. This study evaluated whether positional phenotype influences respiratory outcomes and treatment success in patients treated with MAD. This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 82 consecutive patients with OSA treated with MAD across six tertiary sleep centers. Baseline and follow-up home sleep apnea tests performed at least 6 months after completion of MAD titration were analyzed. POSA was defined according to Cartwright's criteria as a supine apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) at least twice the non-supine AHI. Outcomes included changes in respiratory parameters and treatment success according to Sher's criteria (≥50% AHI reduction and post-treatment AHI <20 events/h). Fifty patients had POSA and 32 had non-POSA. MAD therapy significantly improved total AHI, oxygen desaturation index, and oxygenation parameters in both groups. Treatment success occurred in 42/50 POSA patients (84.0%) and 30/32 non-POSA patients (93.8%; p = 0.332). Reductions in total AHI were also comparable between groups (19.19 ± 15.50 vs 24.14 ± 19.60 events/h; p = 0.232). Likewise, rates of achieving AHI <10 and <5 events/h did not differ significantly between groups. Positional phenotype was not significantly associated with treatment success. MAD therapy was associated with respiratory improvement regardless of positional phenotype. These findings do not support using POSA alone as a criterion for selecting candidates for MAD therapy. Larger prospective studies are required to confirm these results.

papers.title: Adaptive observation-history fusion for EEG-based tracking of PERCLOS-anchored drowsiness.
papers.abstract: This study evaluates explicit adaptive observation-history fusion for continuous EEG-based tracking of PERCLOS-anchored drowsiness and tests whether reward-driven proximal policy optimisation (PPO) provides predictive benefit over supervised fusion and temporal alternatives.Approach. SEED-VIG data from 21 participants and 23 recording sessions were evaluated using strict 21-fold subject-wise leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) validation. In each fold, an EEG encoder generated a PERCLOS-supervised observation proxy, which was recursively combined with the previous estimate through an adaptive observation-history fusion coefficient. Eleven primary methods spanned raw-proxy prediction, conventional filters, supervised and PPO-based fusion, and neural temporal models. Percentage of eyelid closure over time (PERCLOS) provided the ocular-behavioural reference for supervision, PPO reward construction, model selection, and evaluation.Main results. Among methods available in all 21 folds, S4D had the lowest descriptive mean root-mean-square error (RMSE; 0.240746), followed by Gate-7D (0.241490). PPO-7D was available in 20/21 folds. In the prespecified matched comparison (n = 20), the mean RMSE difference (Gate-7D minus PPO-7D) was -0.0022941 (95% bootstrap CI -0.00813595 to 0.00361267; Wilcoxon p = 0.348810), which did not establish a predictive advantage for PPO-7D. None of the 18 broader prespecified PPO-versus-alternative RMSE comparisons met its rejection criterion after Holm correction. Validation-side controlled perturbation altered the EEG-derived proxy, but the prespecified stronger reliability-response criterion was not satisfied.Significance. Explicit observation-history fusion makes the relative contributions of the current EEG proxy and recursive history inspectable. PPO yielded descriptively slower, more persistent fusion-coefficient dynamics than Gate-7D, but its predictive advantage and necessity were not established. The coefficient describes recursive weighting, not calibrated observation reliability.

papers.title: Neural Entropy Pattern : An EEG Representation for Predicting Depression Therapy Outcomes.
papers.abstract: We propose the Neural Entropy Pattern (NEP), an electroencephalography (EEG) representation intended to separate responders from non-responders before treatment. NEP consists of ten entropy measures, computed from 19 channels in five frequency bands and the broadband signal. It was used as a $20 \times 57$ image by twelve deep learning models and as a flat vector by seven shallow classifiers, and was evaluated on a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) dataset ($n = 30$) and a repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) dataset ($n = 61$) under leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) and patient-level five-fold cross-validation, with one prediction per patient and without using the held-out patients for training, early stopping or model selection. The highest balanced accuracy (BA) was, for SSRI, 76.4\% under LOSO (EfficientNet-B0; area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC, 0.89) and 72.2\% under five-fold cross-validation (linear support vector machine, SVM; AUC 0.77) and, for rTMS, 62.1\% ($k$-nearest neighbours; AUC 0.62) and 63.7\% (linear SVM; AUC 0.63). These are the best of 19 models, selected post hoc (95\% confidence intervals 23--32 points). Both SSRI results were above chance by AUC (Holm-adjusted $p = 0.001$ and 0.027). Log-energy and differential entropy carried most of the Shapley-value importance (72\% for SSRI, 60\% for rTMS). For SSRI, the largest group differences were at the left fronto-temporal electrode F7 ($\delta$, $\theta$, $\beta$ and broadband domains; relatively higher power in responders), and the most important features were at F7 and T3 ($\beta$ and $\gamma$ rhythms, broadband signal); for rTMS, the most important features were at the right frontal electrode F4 ($\alpha$ rhythm, broadband signal). The NEP image performed comparably to a multichannel continuous wavelet transform image, and the NEP vector to statistical features.&#xD.

papers.title: Lion Tracks: Protocol for a Microlongitudinal Feasibility Study of Health Behaviors and Emotional Dynamics in Mother-Child Dyads.
papers.abstract: Adolescence is a critical developmental period during which physical activity, sleep, digital-media engagement, cognition, and emotional health become increasingly interconnected. However, reliance on retrospective self-report and low-frequency longitudinal designs limits understanding of how these domains relate within individuals and families in daily life. Few studies have integrated ecological momentary assessment (EMA), passive sensing, and wearable monitoring within mother-child dyads. Lion Tracks aims to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of an integrated ambulatory monitoring protocol. Secondary exploratory aims are to characterize within-person, between-person, and dyadic temporal associations among health behaviors, physiological measures, cognition, and momentary anxiety. Lion Tracks is a prospective, observational, microlongitudinal feasibility study targeting 25 mother-child dyads (50 participants), with children aged 11-14 years. Participants complete baseline assessments, 4 weeks of ambulatory monitoring, and poststudy assessments. Garmin wearables monitor physical activity, sleep, heart rate, and heart rate variability. MetricWire (MetricWire, Inc) collects passive smartphone screen-on duration and timing and delivers repeated EMA of momentary affect, anxiety, context, and behaviors. Digital-media engagement characteristics are self-reported through EMA. Brief mobile cognitive testing assesses cognitive performance. A hybrid EMA design combines fixed, pseudorandom, and behavior-contingent assessments to capture daily experiences while limiting participant burden. Primary outcomes include recruitment, retention, acceptability, participant burden, wearable compliance, EMA completion, and data completeness. Descriptive statistics and CIs will summarize feasibility outcomes. Exploratory multilevel mixed-effects models will examine within-person and between-person associations, while time-lagged and cross-lagged analyses will explore temporal relationships and behavioral synchrony within dyads. The study received approval from The Pennsylvania State University Institutional Review Board (STUDY00027664). Recruitment is ongoing, with 7 mother-child dyads enrolled as of October 2026. Data collection is anticipated to conclude by June 1, 2027. Analyses will follow completion of data collection. Lion Tracks represents Phase 1 of a larger research program designed to progressively optimize ambulatory monitoring and subsequently incorporate mobile electroencephalography to examine neural correlates of daily behaviors, cognition, and emotional functioning. Findings will inform protocol refinement and assess the feasibility of a scalable, multimodal platform for future family-centered behavioral health research. DERR1-10.2196/107879.

papers.title: Measure the Ward First: Intentional Sufficiency as a Design Rule for Sleep Sensing in Acute Inpatient Psychiatry.
papers.abstract: This Viewpoint argues that measurement design, not model capability, is the first constraint on clinical AI in acute inpatient psychiatry and proposes intentional sufficiency as a design rule for sleep sensing on acute wards. Acute psychiatric wards exclude much of the conventional sensing design space: ligature, ingestion, and projectile hazards; unreliable adherence; impaired consent; and nursing workload mean that a device that is excellent when a patient is cooperative may be absent when the patient is most unwell. We define intentional sufficiency in 3 parts: the intended clinical use sets the required signal properties and acceptable error; safety, validity, consent, and workflow constraints define the feasible design space; and within that space, the rule selects the least burdensome option that preserves the required properties, because excess capability can be paid for in persistence, not only in money. We contrast this rule with capability-maximizing design using 2 examples at opposite ends of the design space: a structured nightly nursing sleep duration record that, in Taiwan, already exists within routine care, and a disposable wrist-worn sensing architecture under development that reduces the wearable to what the derived sleep measure requires. The first shows when the rule can conclude that no hardware should be added, provided adequacy has been shown for the intended use; the second shows when it concludes that hardware must be redesigned, and is presented as a design prediction rather than a result. Importantly, agreement with a reference method does not by itself establish task-level sufficiency; greater sensing capability does not necessarily produce more clinically available information when deployment and persistence are constrained; and some signal properties are validity defining and cannot be traded against cost.

papers.title: Differential Impacts of Acoustic Challenge on Three Language-Related Event-Related Brain Potential Components During Speech Processing: Evidence From the N400, the P600, and a Late Frontal Response.
papers.abstract: When listening to acoustically challenging speech, listeners may strategically shift neural resources across multiple language-related cognitive processes in order to compensate for the additional demands. In the current study, we examined the impact of acoustic challenge (via speech-shaped background noise) on three language-related event-related brain potentials (ERPs): the N400 and two late positivities following the N400-a posterior P600 to syntactic violations and a late frontal effect sensitive to word expectancy. Young, normal-hearing adults (N = 48) listened in quiet and in noise (+3 dB SNR speech-shaped stationary noise) to contextually constraining sentences that ended in an expected word, an unexpected word, or a morphosyntactic violation of the expected word, while electroencephalography data were collected. Replicating prior work, we showed that an N400 expectancy effect was both reduced in amplitude and delayed in onset latency in noise. Providing novel insights into late ERP components, we found that a P600 syntax effect was reduced in amplitude by the presence of background noise. We additionally observed that the P600 response was only present for trials in which the listener successfully identified syntactic violations (irrespective of noise). In contrast to the reductions in the N400 and P600, the late frontal response was not reduced in noise. Collectively, this suggests that, while semantic retrieval and syntactic integration may be impaired by acoustic challenge, young, normal-hearing listeners may still prioritize neural resources toward prediction-related processes to help compensate for increased perceptual demands.
papers.journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR

papers.title: Blood pressure and glaucoma.
papers.abstract: Intraocular pressure (IOP) remains the only modifiable risk factor in glaucoma, yet many patients continue to progress despite adequate IOP control. Systemic blood pressure (BP) has re-emerged as a candidate IOP-independent vascular risk factor. This review synthesizes current evidence on the relationship between BP and glaucoma, with particular attention to recent literature describing circadian BP patterns, short- and long-term BP variability, and minimum ambulatory BP values. Both elevated and reduced BP have been associated with glaucoma development and progression, consistent with a bimodal relationship mediated by ocular perfusion pressure. Beyond absolute BP level, recent studies using 24-h ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM) have identified nocturnal over-dipping, high 24-h and long-term BP variability, and, most notably, the minimum BP nadir as independent predictors of structural and functional glaucomatous progression, often outperforming mean BP values in multivariable models. Office-based BP measurements correlate poorly with 24-h ABPM specifically among patients with the lowest BP readings, suggesting isolated office readings may fail to capture clinically relevant hypotensive exposure. Emerging evidence further indicates that BP-related vulnerability is not uniform across the eye: the focal ischemic optic disc phenotype and the central visual field each appear disproportionately susceptible to the effects of low or unstable BP compared with generalized cup enlargement phenotypes or the peripheral field, respectively. The relationship between BP and glaucoma is more complex than a simple linear or threshold-based association, encompassing absolute level, circadian pattern, variability, and minimum values, each of which may independently influence disease course. Twenty-four-hour ABPM may offer meaningful prognostic value beyond office-based measurement, particularly in patients progressing despite controlled IOP, and clinicians should maintain a low threshold to pursue such monitoring and to coordinate BP management with primary care or cardiology colleagues in this population.

papers.title: Performance-Based Evolution of Near-Infrared Serotonin Nanosensors from DNA-Wrapped Carbon Nanotube Libraries.
papers.abstract: Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5HT) is an important neurotransmitter involved in the regulation of mood, appetite, and sleep, and its dysregulation has been associated with disorders such as depression and Parkinson's disease. Selective molecular tools that can distinguish 5HT from other neurochemicals are essential for advancing both neurochemistry and disease-related research. However, conventional analytical methods are labor-intensive and sometimes suffer from poor discrimination among closely related neurotransmitters. In this study, we developed a near-infrared fluorescent 5HT nanosensor based on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA)-wrapped single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) using a performance-based systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (pSELEC) strategy. Unlike conventional affinity-focused selection, this approach prioritized fluorescence modulation as the screening output and combined high-throughput microarray printing with automated fluorescence imaging to evaluate more than 108 ssDNA-SWCNT configurations. After characterizing the enriched DNA candidates, Seq6 was selected as a lead scaffold and underwent post-selection engineering, including covalent modification with a quencher dye and co-wrapping with spacer ssDNA. A methylene blue-conjugated Seq6 produced a "turn-off" fluorescence response to 5HT together with an opposite-direction response to dopamine (DA), providing improved discrimination between the two analytes. These findings demonstrate that pSELEC is a useful strategy for developing sensitive and selective near-infrared nanosensors for real-time neurotransmitter sensing.

papers.title: Combined Prenatal Environmental Stressors Induce Suprachiasmatic Degeneration with Unexpected Behavioural Resilience in Long-Evans Rats.
papers.abstract: Environmental heat stress and displacement adversity during pregnancy pose significant risks to neurodevelopment, particularly in regions with high maternal mortality and population displacement. The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), the brain's master circadian pacemaker, is vulnerable to prenatal environmental insults, yet the combined impact of thermal and psychosocial stressors on SCN development remains unexplored. We examined the effects of prenatal heat stress and displacement-like conditions on SCN morphology and behaviour across two critical developmental stages. Twenty-five timed-pregnant Long-Evans rats were exposed to heat stress (38-40°C, 2 h daily), displacement conditions (overnight food/water restriction plus overcrowding), combined stressors, or control conditions from gestational days 15-20. Male offspring were assessed at postnatal days 10 (neonatal) and 30 (juvenile). Heat exposure induced significant maternal hyperthermia (2.5-2.9°C elevation). Histological analysis revealed marked SCN cellular degeneration across stress groups at both developmental stages, characterised by reduced cell counts, pyknotic nuclei, and disrupted tissue architecture. Despite structural damage, juvenile behavioural testing revealed paradoxical outcomes: combined stress exposure reduced anxiety-like behaviour in the elevated plus maze, enhanced sociability in three-chamber testing, while preserving recognition memory. Growth analysis demonstrated preferential brain sparing despite reduced somatic growth, with significantly elevated brain-to-body weight ratios in stress-exposed animals. These findings demonstrate that prenatal environmental stressors cause lasting damage to the SCN but trigger adaptive behavioural responses. The dissociation between structural vulnerability and functional adaptation suggests complex neurodevelopmental programming with implications for populations experiencing heat exposure and displacement adversity.

papers.title: Haze and health: a mixed method approach exploring physical and psychological challenges of smog faced by university employees in Pakistan.
papers.abstract: The present study was designed to explore the role of smog on the physical and psychological health of university employees in Lahore, Pakistan, during November 2024. A mixed-methods approach was designed to assess the relationship between perceived air quality, psychological distress (depression, anxiety, stress), and physical symptoms (respiratory, digestive, sleep disturbances, headaches) in university employees. Study 1 was a cross-sectional survey of 350 university employees to assess the relationship between study variables. Results indicate a significant positive relationship between poor air quality, psychological and physical symptoms. In study 2, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 employees, exploring their exposure to smog and its impact on their physical and psychological health and the coping strategies they use to overcome these impacts. Thematic analysis highlighted greater vulnerability among older employees and those with preexisting conditions. Challenges included respiratory and cardiovascular issues, increased stress, cognitive impairments, and reduced productivity. Institutional shortcomings like inflexible policies worsened impacts. Recommended interventions include remote work, improved indoor air quality, and mental health support to alleviate these challenges and enhance well-being.

papers.title: Coevolving gene networks underlying a phenotypic syndrome revealed via integrating comparative genomic and microevolutionary analyses.
papers.abstract: Complex adaptive traits often comprise interacting, coevolving phenotypes that together for a syndrome that is shaped by multiple genetic loci. While using intraspecific variation is an established approach for investigating syndromes, such polymorphism typically captures only a subset of syndrome traits. Diapause, an alternative developmental pathway that evolved independently in many species to synchronize life cycles with resource availability, exemplifies this challenge. While subsets of this essential phenotype have long been studied at a single species level, the genomic basis of the full diapause syndrome remains poorly understood. This paucity of insights has fueled a long-standing debate about how life cycle synchronization evolves and whether convergent phenotypes employ shared mechanisms. Using a comparative genomic analysis spanning diverse diapause transitions in butterflies, we identified a large network of coevolving genes unique to diapausing species. The network is composed of functional modules spanning circadian regulation, metabolism, and cell cycle control. We tested whether this macroevolutionary scale network predicts microevolutionary dynamics, hypothesizing that this network is the polygenic architecture underlying the diapause syndrome. Analyses revealed that allelic variation in the diapause network is significantly enriched in signatures of local adaptation across latitudes, but only in diapausing species. Thus, we empirically show that diapause evolves through modular, coevolving gene networks, components of which impact intraspecific variation in diapause. Using this integrative perspective on a complex phenotype opens a horizon of inquiry for understanding seasonal adaptation across evolutionary scales, while demonstrating the power of integrating comparative genomics with microevolutionary dynamics to dissect complex phenotypic syndromes.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: Co-translational surveillance of nascent polypeptides times circadian rhythms in Drosophila.
papers.abstract: Ribosome-associated quality control (RQC) ensures proteostasis by actively degrading aberrant translation intermediates on stalled ribosomes, yet its physiological role in gene regulation remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate that Drosophila circadian clocks employ RQC to sustain 24-h behavioral rhythms. RNA interference-mediated depletion of RQC components in circadian pacemaker neurons impaired free-running locomotor rhythms. In particular, the loss of Caliban (Clbn) function in clearing 60S-associated faulty polypeptides led to weak but long-period rhythms in adult locomotor activity. These behavioral phenotypes were accompanied by delayed accumulation of the core clock protein PERIOD (PER), most evidently in pigment-dispersing factor-expressing clock neurons, and dampened structural plasticity of their axons. per heterozygosity exaggerated CLBN depletion-induced period lengthening, whereas overexpression of the PER-associating factor TIMELESS blunted this effect. Clbn deficiency in Drosophila S2R+ cell cultures increased the generation of prematurely terminated PER species, particularly when PER translation is high, and sensitized full-length PER to phosphorylation-dependent decay. These findings support PER as a clock-relevant RQC substrate, providing a mechanistic link between translation flux, co-translational surveillance, and circadian timekeeping.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: Adapting Tensor Kernel Machines to Enable Efficient Transfer Learning for Seizure Detection.
papers.abstract: Transfer learning aims to optimize performance in a target task by learning from a related source problem. In this work, we propose an efficient transfer learning method using a tensor kernel machine. Our method takes inspiration from the adaptive SVM and hence transfers 'knowledge' from the source to the 'adapted' model via regularization. The main advantage of using tensor kernel machines is that they leverage low-rank tensor networks to learn a compact non-linear model in the primal domain. This allows for a more efficient adaptation without adding more parameters to the model. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, we apply the adaptive tensor kernel machine (Adapt-TKM) to seizure detection on behind-the-ear EEG. By personalizing patient-independent models with a small amount of patient-specific data, the patient-adapted model (which utilizes the Adapt-TKM), improves the detection performance for the majority of the patients and significantly outperforms the fully patient-specific model. Notably, it is able to do so while requiring around 100 times fewer parameters than the adaptive SVM model, leading to a correspondingly faster inference speed. This makes the Adapt-TKM especially useful for resource-constrained wearable devices.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society

papers.title: Cross-Attention Estimation of Asynchronous EEG Functional Networks for Affective Disorder Characterization.
papers.abstract: Existing EEG functional network methods have provided important insights into affective disorders, but the direction, timing, and modulation of inter-regional influences are not fully characterized within a unified representation. To address this limitation, we propose an attention-based framework for interpretable modeling of asynchronous functional brain networks (aFBNs) from a causal-discovery perspective. Its Cross-Attention Causal Discovery (CACD) module jointly estimates directed influence strength, transmission delay, and modulation sign from multivariate EEG. CACD integrates a dual-branch decoder for separating intra- and inter-channel dynamics, a learnable cross-attention mask for connection selection, and an Attention-Gradient Consistency (AGC) mechanism for improving attribution consistency and delay localization. Experiments on nine causal discovery benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of CACD in recovering causal structures and estimating transmission delays. On three clinical EEG datasets, the framework achieves competitive subject-independent classification performance and reveals neurophysiologically plausible asynchronous connectivity patterns. Delay and modulation information provide additional discriminative value beyond directed influence strength. Together, these findings support aFBNs as an interpretable representation for characterizing affective-disorder-related neural dynamics.

papers.title: Self-reported decreased libido in patients evaluated for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA): Association with depressive symptoms rather than OSA severity.
papers.abstract: BackgroundSexual health complaints are frequently reported by patients evaluated for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) but remain under-recognized in respiratory care settings. The relative contributions of respiratory disease severity, daytime symptoms, and psychological factors to decreased libido in this population remain poorly understood.ObjectivesThe aim of the study was to determine the prevalence of self-reported decreased libido in patients evaluated for suspected or confirmed OSA and to identify factors independently associated with this complaint.DesignMonocentric cross-sectional observational study performed in patients referred for suspected or confirmed obstructive sleep apnea from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025.MethodsSelf-reported decreased libido was assessed using a dichotomous patient-reported measure. Demographic characteristics, body mass index, comorbidities, OSA severity indices, daytime sleepiness, fatigue, and depressive symptoms were collected using standardized clinical assessments and questionnaires. Multivariable logistic regression models were performed to identify factors independently associated with decreased libido, including models based on directed acyclic graph (DAG) confounder selection, extended models including symptoms, sex-stratified analyses, and formal testing of sex-by-depression interaction.ResultsAmong 188 included patients (mean age 55.3 ± 15.9 years; 64.4% women), self-reported decreased libido was reported by 44.7%. In multivariable analyses based on DAG-selected confounders, increasing age was independently associated with decreased libido, while moderate-to-severe OSA showed only a borderline association. In the extended model including daytime symptoms and depressive symptoms, higher depressive symptom scores remained independently associated with decreased libido, whereas indices of OSA severity, daytime sleepiness, and fatigue were not associated. Sex-stratified analyses showed that depressive symptoms and relationship status were associated with decreased libido among women, whereas age was the main determinant among men. Formal testing of the interaction between sex and depressive symptoms was not statistically significant.ConclusionsSelf-reported decreased libido is common among patients evaluated for suspected OSA. Decreased libido appears to be more consistently associated with depressive symptoms and psychosocial factors than with objective respiratory disease severity. These findings highlight the importance of integrating psychological and quality-of-life assessment into routine respiratory care pathways for patients evaluated for OSA.

papers.title: Reinforced hippocampus-accumbens pathway marks a shift toward cognitive decline in aging.
papers.abstract: Aging triggers early functional alterations in brain circuits preceding cognitive impairment, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unaddressed. Spatial navigation and memory, among the earliest affected, depend on the hippocampus and downstream targets such as the nucleus accumbens (NAc), which integrates spatial and motivational information to guide goal-directed behaviors. Here we identify age-related, sex-dependent changes in the dorsal hippocampus-NAc (dHPC→NAc) pathway. Combining optogenetics with electrophysiology, chemogenetics, and behavioral analyses in mice, we show that aging shifts the excitation-inhibition balance in dorsal CA1 toward pyramidal neuron hyperactivity, strengthening hippocampal outputs. This selectively enhances synaptic drive onto D1 receptor-expressing medium spiny neurons and involves a previously unrecognized long-range parvalbumin-expressing projection. Chemogenetically reducing the dHPC→NAc activity improves memory in aged mice. In humans, fMRI reveals heightened posterior hippocampal activity and stronger posterior HPC-NAc coupling during navigation. Together, we uncover a targetable pathway acting in an intervention-sensitive window of aging to correct negative cognitive trajectories.

papers.title: Cool nights attenuate morning OsRLCK309 expression and compromise blast resistance in rice.
papers.abstract: Nighttime cooling during day-night thermocycles has long been associated with increased rice blast severity, yet the host mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we show that cool-night pre-exposure weakens subsequent blast resistance in rice under a common post-inoculation regime and is associated with reduced morning expression of a receptor-like cytoplasmic kinase (RLCK)-enriched gene set. We identify OsRLCK309, a cool-night-responsive receptor-like cytoplasmic kinase, as a positive regulator of blast resistance and pattern-triggered immunity (PTI), including chitin-induced reactive oxygen species production, mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) activation, and Ca2+ influx. OsRLCK309 associates with the chitin co-receptor kinase CHITIN ELICITOR RECEPTOR KINASE 1 (OsCERK1), and OsCERK1-mediated phosphorylation of OsRLCK309 at Ser245 and Thr246 contributes to full activation of defense against rice blast. Under warm nights, CIRCADIAN CLOCK ASSOCIATED 1 (OsCCA1) promotes a morning-phased expression peak of OsRLCK309. Cool nights attenuate this OsCCA1-associated morning peak and induce dehydration-responsive element-binding protein 1A (OsDREB1A), which activates the OsRLCK309 promoter and contributes to its nighttime induction under cool-night conditions. In transgenic complementation lines, mutation of the two OsDREB1A-binding sites in the OsRLCK309 promoter attenuated cool-night-responsive transcriptional redistribution and was associated with reduced disease severity after cool-night pre-exposure, with minimal detectable agronomic trade-offs under our conditions. These results support a thermocycle-sensitive model linking night-temperature history to transcriptional timing, receptor-proximal immune signaling, and blast disease in rice, and suggest that modification of the DREB-binding motifs in the OsRLCK309 promoter may help maintain blast resistance under variable night temperatures.

papers.title: Circadian disruption worsens postseptic pulmonary fibrotic remodeling through a CLOCK/PIEZO1-linked myeloid immunometabolic program.
papers.abstract: Whether circadian rhythm disruption (CRD) promotes fibrotic remodeling after septic lung injury remains unclear. We tested whether CRD drives this process through macrophage CLOCK-PIEZO1 signaling. Lung specimens from patients with sepsis-associated lung injury and non-injured controls were analyzed alongside public murine lung transcriptomic datasets. Mice underwent cecal ligation and puncture or sham surgery and were maintained under stable or repeatedly shifted light-dark cycles; selected experiments included LysM-lineage Piezo1 deletion. Day-3 lung injury and day-28 fibrosis were assessed, and mechanisms were defined using genetic, biochemical and co-culture approaches. CRD suppressed CLOCK expression in macrophage-lineage cells, leading to increased PIEZO1 expression and aggravated collagen deposition. CLOCK repressed Piezo1 transcription through a promoter E-box. Loss of myeloid Clock reduced Clock mesor and amplitude by 66.3% and 90.3%, respectively, increased Piezo1 mesor by 54.0%, and produced genotype-by-rhythm interactions for both genes (P < 0.0001). PIEZO1 activation impaired lysosomal acid lipase (LAL)-dependent lipophagy and promoted ZDHHC19-mediated peptidylarginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) palmitoylation and extracellular-trap formation. LysM-lineage Piezo1 deletion attenuated fibrosis. PIEZO1 inhibition or DNase I reduced epithelial injury and fibroblast activation induced by extracellular DNA-rich macrophage signals. CRD promotes post-septic fibrosis through a CLOCK-PIEZO1-linked macrophage immunometabolic program, identifying PIEZO1, extracellular DNA-rich traps and impaired lipid clearance as candidate targets.

papers.title: Social jet lag in CPAP-treated cohorts: distribution, age gradients, and weekend rebound.
papers.abstract: Social jet lag (SJL), the discrepancy in sleep timing between work and free nights, reflects schedule-related timing misalignment. We characterized CPAP-derived SJL in treated obstructive sleep apnea and assessed its distribution, behavioral correlates, age pattern, and consistency across two independent clinical cohorts. We analyzed longitudinal CPAP use timing from Rutgers-RWJ Health (RWJ, N = 1415) and Hackensack Meridian Health (HMH, N = 1497), with a combined analytic cohort of 2912 patients. Patients had at least 31 valid nights and at least one valid work night and free night. Mid-sleep on work (MSW) and free nights (MSF) was estimated using circular statistics. SJL was categorized as none (< 1 h), moderate (1-2 h), or severe (≥ 2 h). Work and free night CPAP use duration, free night rebound, age-stratified prevalence, and site consistency were assessed. In the combined cohort, SJL was right-skewed, with a median of 0.43 h [IQR 0.19-0.82]; 17.8% had SJL > 1 h, including 14.8% with moderate and 3.0% with severe SJL. Greater SJL was associated with shorter work night CPAP use duration, later free night timing, and greater free night rebound. SJL prevalence was highest among adults aged 26-50 years and declined progressively with age. Similar patterns at RWJ and HMH supported the robustness of the combined findings. CPAP-derived SJL was generally modest but identified a meaningful subgroup with work-free differences in CPAP use timing. Routinely collected CPAP records may provide a scalable, low-burden screening measure to identify patients whose work-free timing patterns warrant further behavioral or circadian assessment. CURRENT KNOWLEDGE/STUDY RATIONALE: Standard CPAP reports focus on adherence, residual respiratory events, mask leak, and pressure but provide limited information about sleep timing or weekday-weekend schedule regularity. Social jet lag may contribute to residual symptoms in treated obstructive sleep apnea, but it is not routinely measured in clinical CPAP workflows. This study shows that routinely collected CPAP adherence data can be used to estimate social jet lag, weekday sleep restriction, free night rebound, and age-related sleep timing patterns across two independent clinical cohorts. CPAP-derived social jet lag may provide a scalable screening phenotype to identify patients who warrant further behavioral, circadian, or activity-based assessment.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine

papers.title: Analysis of nighttime heart rate variability during rapid eye movement and non-rapid eye movement in OSA.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a heterogeneous condition. However, many inconsistencies remain regarding the analysis of heart rate variability (HRV) and autonomic nervous system (ANS) function differences among patients with rapid eye movement (REM)-related OSA, nonrapid eye movement (NREM)-related OSA during different sleep periods. This retrospective study included 373 patients with OSA who completed polysomnography (PSG) at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University from May 2023 to February 2024. Patients were classified into REM-related OSA (REM-OSA), NREM-related OSA (NREM-OSA), and non-stage-specific OSA groups according to PSG. Clinical demographics, PSG parameters, and HRV indices were compared across the three groups. Multivariable regression models were constructed to examine the independent associations of AHI and OSA phenotype with HRV, adjusting for age, gender, BMI, and segment duration. A total of 373 OSA patients were included (120 REM-OSA, 90 NREM-OSA, and 163 non-stage-specific OSA). In female patients with mild-to-moderate OSA, no significant differences in HRV were observed across the three phenotypes. In male patients with mild-to-moderate OSA, the REM-OSA group exhibited lower LFnu and LF/HF and higher HFnu during N1 and N2 sleep compared with the other phenotypes. During REM sleep, the REM-OSA group showed higher SDNN than the NREM-OSA group. In patients with severe OSA, the non-stage-specific group showed lower SDNN, RMSSD, and pNN50 during REM sleep than the NREM-OSA group. Multivariate regression showed that AHI was significantly associated with frequency-domain HRV indices across all sleep stages. After adjusting for age, gender, BMI, and segment duration, the REM-OSA phenotype was independently associated with lower LFnu and LF/HF and higher HFnu during N1 and N2 sleep, but not during REM sleep (explaining 8.6%-24.7% of variance). The autonomic effects of REM-OSA are sex-dependent and severity-dependent. In male patients with mild-to-moderate OSA, the REM-OSA phenotype was associated with relative parasympathetic dominance during N1 and N2 sleep, but not during REM sleep. ANS function may not be the primary mechanism linking REM-OSA to cardiovascular risk, and the autonomic profile of REM-OSA is more nuanced than previously recognized.

papers.title: Sex and photoperiod shape depot-specific adipose tissue remodelling and metabolic signalling in diet-induced obese Fischer 344 rats.
papers.abstract: Sex and photoperiod are major regulators of metabolic homeostasis, yet their combined associations with adipose tissue remodelling under obesogenic conditions remain poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate how sex and photoperiod jointly relate to adipose tissue morphology and function. Male and female Fischer 344 rats were fed a cafeteria diet for 11 weeks and exposed to either long-day (18 h light/day, L18) or short-day (6 h light/day, L6) photoperiods during the last 8 weeks. Males exhibited greater body weight gain, total fat mass and insulin resistance than females, particularly under L18. In subcutaneous adipose tissue, remodelling was primarily associated with sex, with females displaying a higher number of smaller adipocytes, consistent with hyperplastic expansion, whereas males showed larger adipocytes consistent with hypertrophy. Visceral depots were analysed separately within each sex because male eWAT and female oWAT are sex-specific depots. In both tissues, L6 was associated with higher adipocyte number and smaller cell size, whereas L18 was associated with a more hypertrophic pattern. Gene expression analysis revealed depot-specific responses, with adipogenic and lipid metabolism genes showing predominantly sex-associated differences in subcutaneous fat, whereas photoperiod-associated transcriptional changes were observed in visceral depots. Notably, photoperiod-associated changes in Sucnr1 gene expression occurred in opposite directions in eWAT and oWAT. Overall, these findings indicate that sex and photoperiod are associated with adipose tissue remodelling in a depot-specific manner.

papers.title: Transforming growth factor beta 1 (TGF-β1) putatively modulates central noradrenergic neurotransmission via a TGF-β receptor type 1 (TGF-βR1)-mediated mechanism in male rats.
papers.abstract: Transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) signaling has been implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders, but its direct electrophysiological effects on central monoaminergic neurons remain unclear. This study examined whether TGF-β1 modulates serotonergic, dopaminergic, and noradrenergic neuronal activity in vivo. Adult male rats received acute TGF-β1 administration, and extracellular single-unit recordings were performed from serotonergic neurons in the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN), dopaminergic neurons in the ventral tegmental area (VTA), and noradrenergic neurons in the locus coeruleus (LC). Additional experiments assessed the involvement of noradrenergic neurotransmission using fusaric acid-induced noradrenaline depletion and the role of TGF-β receptor type I (TGF-βR1) using the antagonist LY2109761. TGF-β1 did not significantly alter the firing activity of DRN serotonergic neurons or VTA dopaminergic neurons. In contrast, TGF-β1 significantly reduced the spontaneous firing activity and burst parameters of LC noradrenergic neurons. Noradrenaline depletion with fusaric acid abolished the inhibitory effect of TGF-β1 on LC neuronal activity. Conversely, pharmacological blockade of TGF-βR1 with LY2109761 increased LC neuronal firing, suggesting that endogenous TGF-β1 signaling exerts a tonic inhibitory influence on the noradrenergic system. These findings identify TGF-β1/TGF-βR1 signaling as a selective modulator of central noradrenergic neuronal activity. The apparent involvement of noradrenergic signaling in the suppression of LC firing may represent a mechanism linking TGF-β1 signaling with monoaminergic circuits involved in stress regulation and affective disorders.

papers.title: Association between breakfast frequency, school commuting mode, and psychological symptoms: a cross-sectional study of Chinese adolescents.
papers.abstract: Psychological symptoms among adolescents are a rising global public health concern. Irregular breakfast habits and passive commuting may be associated with these symptoms, but large-scale national evidence from China is scarce. We examined independent and joint associations using nationwide Chinese adolescent data. A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to June 2025 among 52,035 adolescents aged 12-17 (26,104 boys, 25,931 girls) from 27 regions in China, using a multistage stratified cluster random sampling. Breakfast frequency and school commuting mode (active: walking or cycling; passive: motorized transport) were assessed via self-report questionnaires. Subclinical psychological symptoms were evaluated using the Multidimensional Subhealth Questionnaire for Adolescents (MSQA). Covariates included age, sex, monthly household income, sleep duration, body mass index, and grip strength. t-tests, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression are used to explore the associations. The proportions of adolescents breakfast frequency ≤ 1, 2-4, and > 4 times per week were 4.0%, 12.5%, and 83.4% and active and passive commuting accounted for 43.1% and 56.9%. The prevalence of emotional problems, behavioral problems, social adjustment difficulties, and subclinical psychological symptoms were 27.5%, 26.6%, 17.6%, and 20.8%. Fully adjusted models found independent associations of low breakfast frequency (≤ 1/week: OR 2.58, 95%CI 2.35-2.82) and passive commuting (OR 1.18, 95%CI 1.13-1.24) with symptoms; the combined category had the highest OR (OR 3.04, 95%CI 2.66-3.49, P < 0.001). Low breakfast frequency and passive commuting were associated with higher prevalence of subclinical psychological symptoms, with the highest OR in the combined category but no evidence of multiplicative interaction. Related interventions warrant evaluation. • Low breakfast frequency and passive school commuting are separately associated with adverse psychological outcomes in adolescents, but large nationwide evidence from China is limited. • The joint association of these two modifiable daily behaviors with adolescent psychological symptoms remains unclear, including whether the association of one behavior varies according to the other. • This large nationwide study found independent associations of low breakfast frequency and passive commuting with higher odds of subclinical psychological symptoms among Chinese adolescents. • Adolescents with infrequent breakfast consumption and passive commuting had the highest odds of psychological symptoms, with no statistical evidence of multiplicative interaction.

papers.title: Influence of social housing on dim light at night induced behavioural and hepatic alterations in mice.
papers.abstract: Circadian disruption induced by dim light at night (DLAN) is increasingly recognised as an environmental stressor that adversely affects behavioural and metabolic physiology. While social interaction is known to buffer stress responses, whether it mitigates DLAN-induced behavioural and hepatic dysfunction remains poorly understood. Therefore, this study investigated the influence of social housing on behavioural, oxidative and hepatic alterations induced by chronic DLAN exposure in male mice. Sixty-four mice were assigned to four experimental groups comprising group-housed and socially isolated animals maintained under either a standard light-dark cycle or DLAN for 28 days. Behavioural assessments were performed to evaluate anxiety-like behaviour and anhedonia, followed by histological examination of the liver and biochemical analyses of antioxidant enzyme activities, glucose and hepatic function biomarkers. DLAN exposure increased anxiety-like behaviour, anhedonia, oxidative stress and hepatic dysfunction, with these effects being most pronounced in socially isolated mice. Histological analyses revealed marked hepatocellular degeneration and lipid accumulation in isolated DLAN-exposed animals, accompanied by reduced catalase and superoxide dismutase activities and elevated glucose, triglyceride and hepatic enzyme levels. In contrast, group-housed mice exposed to DLAN exhibited significantly attenuated behavioural deficits, improved antioxidant status and reduced hepatic injury compared with their socially isolated counterparts. These findings demonstrate that social housing alleviates DLAN-induced behavioural and hepatic dysfunction, highlighting the importance of social interaction as a modulator of physiological resilience during circadian disruption.
papers.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology

papers.title: Intermittent Hypoxia Induces Epigenetic Changes and p16-Mediated Senescence in Vascular Dysfunction in Male Mice.
papers.abstract: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a pervasive cardiovascular risk factor linked to accelerated aging. We investigated the underlying tissue-specific and systemic epigenetic mechanisms and the role of cellular senescence in the pathophysiology of OSA and associated cardiovascular disease (CVD). C57BL/6J male mice were exposed to intermittent hypoxia (IH) or room air (RA) (n=25 mice/group) for 7 to 210 days. DNA methylation profiling was conducted on left cardiac ventricle and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and the impact of IH duration was studied using regression models. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) was calculated using a multi-tissue epigenetic clock. The role of p16-mediated senescence in IH-induced vascular dysfunction was assessed using transgenic mouse models (n=8 mice/group). IH exposures increased blood pressure and altered endothelial function in male mice. IH/RA differentially methylated positions (DMPs) were identified in left cardiac ventricle (n=5,747) and PBMCs (n=1,307), with minimal overlap (n=163, p=8.03 x 10-8). Both tissues differed in the EAA trajectory throughout the exposures. Epigenetic changes linked to cardiac dysfunction and cellular senescence, highlighting the Cdkn2a gene (encoding the p16 protein, a marker of cellular senescence). p16 expression was increased in aortic endothelial cells following IH. Systemic ablation of p16-expressing cells reversed IH-induced hypertension and restored coronary flow reserve. IH induces duration-dependent, tissue-specific epigenetic dysregulation and accelerated biological aging with p16-mediated cellular senescence as a primary driver. Targeting the senescent endothelium can revert OSA-induced vascular dysfunction, thereby establishing a novel mechanistic framework for cellular senescence as a therapeutic target in OSA.

papers.title: Optimizing the management of obstructive sleep apnea with pharmacotherapy.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects up to 1 billion people worldwide. Despite availability of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy as the main treatment modality, a need for additional pharmacologic agents remains. Pharmacologic therapies can help improve patient symptoms of sleepiness and address the underlying mechanisms (endotypes) of disordered breathing in patients with OSA. Potential pharmacologic target therapy of the four main OSA endotypes, airway collapsibility, poor upper airway muscle dilation, high loop gain, and low arousal threshold, are reviewed. Medications to help with daytime sleepiness are also discussed. Both original research and review articles spanning 2000 to 2026 are included in this review. Published articles were identified through PubMed and in-progress studies were identified through field experts. The current landscape of pharmacologic options for OSA is very exciting, especially with the expansion in number of agents addressing obesity that also help improve airway collapsibility. However, many of these therapies (apart from anti-obesity medications and medications for daytime sleepiness) are still experimental. Further evaluation is required before many of these pharmacologic agents are officially approved for use with or without CPAP. Agents addressing specific endotypes will pave the way for more personalized OSA treatment.

papers.title: Reading the night between the epochs: continuous decoding of sleep microstructure.
Quantity and quality of children's screen use and their neural and associated behavioral outcomes: A systematic review.
papers.abstract: The developmental impact of screen use on young children remains an active area of inquiry, with evidence of both risks and benefits depending on quantity and quality of exposure. This systematic review synthesized 23 neuroimaging studies of children aged 0-8 years, selected from 19,699 records identified across PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and APA PsycINFO (2012-2025). Studies were included if they examined typically developing children, employed neuroimaging methods (EEG, fNIRS, or MRI), and assessed the effects of digital media exposure or intervention on brain and associated outcomes. Eight studies on quantity associated greater screen exposure with lower prefrontal activation, altered cortical activity, differences in white matter pathways, and lower myelination in language and cognitive regions. Fifteen studies on quality found that interactive and multimodal media, educational gamification, and caregiver co-use enhanced networks supporting language, perception, and socioemotional skills, whereas non-educational media showed null effects. Our paper argues that discussions on screen use should move beyond the sole focus on duration of screen-time to consider the dimensions of design, content, and context of media use and how they may shape developmental outcomes.

papers.title: The Sequence of Photoperiod Exposure Determines Hypocotyl Development in Arabidopsis Seedlings.
papers.abstract: Sensing and responding to photoperiod changes is essential for plants to adapt to the changing seasons. The elongation of the hypocotyl, the seedling stem, is directly controlled by the photoperiod through a coincidence model. However, these models were built on observations from growth under a static photoperiod. It is unknown if changes in the duration of the photoperiod during development influence hypocotyl elongation. To investigate this, we designed a photoperiod shift assay where seedlings were exposed to an initial photoperiod before being moved to a second photoperiod. Whilst hypocotyl elongation primarily coincided with exposure to the second photoperiod, we found that photoperiod exposure earlier in development also influenced final hypocotyl length. The response to these photoperiod shifts was dependent on the Arabidopsis ecotype, the ambient temperature of the growth assay and the developmental age of the seedling when exposed to the photoperiod shift. We also found that phyB and ELF3 have a critical role in responding to the photoperiod shift. It is unclear if the activity of phyB and ELF3 is circadian clock-dependent, as the circadian clock quickly re-phased to the second photoperiod. This suggests that additional mechanisms contribute to integrating photoperiod information across development. In summary, our work has revealed that the integration of photoperiodic information during seedling emergence and early development determines hypocotyl elongation.

papers.title: Nucleocytoplasmic protein partitioning in plant circadian and plant photobiological processes.
papers.abstract: All nuclear proteins require some mechanism to facilitate import from the cytosol into the nucleus. Additionally, many proteins are dually localized, with specific functions and partners within the two compartments. While karyopherins (importins/exportins) generally underlie the basic mechanism of nucleocytoplasmic partitioning, how the members of this large protein family are exploited in specific instances has remained unclear. In this review we survey and update the known instances and mechanisms of nucleocytoplasmic partitioning of plant photoreceptors and proteins associated with the plant circadian clock. We identify some mechanisms shared among different protein species which help establish nuclear and cytosolic pools appropriate to their developmental and physiological roles and identify new or lesser known ways of achieving nucleocytoplasmic protein balance.

papers.title: Transvenous Lead Extraction, Venous Obstruction, and the Superior Vena Cava.
Sex-specific differences in mortality in obstructive sleep apnea: results from the Sleep Apnea Patients in Skaraborg (SIS) Study.
papers.abstract: Sex differences in mortality among patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) remain incompletely understood. We analyzed data from the Sleep Apnea Patients in Skaraborg (SIS) Study, including adult patients with OSA defined as an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥5 events/hour. OSA severity was classified as mild (AHI 5-14.9), moderate (AHI 15-29.9) or severe (AHI ≥30). All-cause mortality was assessed over a median follow-up of 5.9 (interquartile range 4.6-7.2) years using multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, obesity, current smoking status, diabetes mellitus, Epworth Sleepiness Scale score, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and cerebrovascular disease. Interaction between sex and OSA severity was tested, and analyses were stratified by age (≤50 and >50 years). The cohort comprised 3,843 patients with 421 deaths. Despite lower OSA severity, women had an overall mortality of 10.0% (120/1,203), compared with 11.4% (301/2,640) in men. Men had higher mortality than women in severe OSA (HR 1.50; 95% confidence interval (CI) [1.09; 2.05]; p = 0.011), whereas no sex differences were observed in mild and moderate OSA (HR 0.95; 95% CI [0.61; 1.50]; p = 0.850 and 1.09; 95%CI [0.73; 1.63]; p = 0.662; interaction p = 0.110) . In age-stratified analyses, among patients ≤50 years, women demonstrated higher mortality than men irrespective of the severity of OSA (HR for men versus women 0.34; 95%CI [0.14; 0.87]; p = 0.024), while among patients >50 years, men with severe OSA had the highest mortality risk (HR 1.58; 95%CI [1.15; 2.18]; p = 0.005). Treatment was associated with reduced mortality in patients >50 years (HR 0.52; 95%CI [0.40; 0.67]; p < 0.001). Mortality risk among patients with OSA varied according to sex, age, and OSA severity. Our findings suggest potentially distinct risk patterns, with higher mortality observed among younger women and among older men with severe OSA. The findings in younger patients should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of events.
